short_comment: LaPorta caught one of four targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munch.
long_comment: The Lions didn't need to throw it much, as Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game for the Patriots early, and LaPorta simply didn't get many chances to make an impact. It was the worst performance of the season for the fourth-year tight end, but LaPorta's gone four straight games without reaching 40 receiving yards or getting into the end zone. He'll try to break out in Week 11 against the Buccaneers.

short_comment: Williams caught four of seven targets for 50 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich.
long_comment: Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs monopolized the Lions' offense on the day, scoring four of the team's five TDs, and there wasn't much production left over for Williams. The fifth-year wideout has topped 50 receiving yards just three times this season, and he'll take a 32-518-5 line on 51 targets through nine games into a Week 11 battle with the Buccaneers.

short_comment: St. Brown caught four of five targets for 98 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich.
long_comment: The Lions didn't need to throw it much, as Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game for the Patriots early. St. Brown took full advantage of the volume he saw however, scoring on a 56-yard catch and run in the first quarter and then taking another short pass from Jared Goff and turning it into a 28-yard TD in the third. It was St. Brown's third multi-TD game of the season but his first since Week 2, and he'll take a 65-755-7 line on 91 targets through nine games into a Week 11 clash with the Buccaneers.

short_comment: Bates made all five of his PATs in the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich.
long_comment: Bates did not attempt a field goal in the contest. He remains 16-for-17 on field-goal attempts and moves to 29-for-29 on PATs through nine regular-season games in 2026.

short_comment: TeSlaa caught two of five targets for 19 yards and a touchdown during the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich. He also recorded a tackle.
long_comment: It was a quiet day for TeSlaa, with the Lions' offense being powered by usual suspects Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs, with the latter duo combining for four touchdowns (three receiving, one rushing). TeSlaa was the other Lions player to find the end zone, which took place early in the second quarter on a 12-yard touchdown pass from Jared Goff. It was the first touchdown catch of the season for TeSlaa, who found the end zone six times across 17 regular-season games during his rookie campaign in 2025. He has been the Lions' distant WR3 behind St. Brown and Jameson Williams, and that shouldn't change ahead of the team's Week 11 tilt against the Buccaneers on Nov. 22.

short_comment: Vaki turned six carries into 28 yards and added a 17-yard catch on his only target during the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich.
long_comment: Lead back Jahmyr Gibbs dominated with 252 yards and three touchdowns on 29 total touches (22 carries, seven catches on eight targets), but Vaki also had his moments during Sunday's game, including a 17-yard catch on the first play of the second quarter. Vaki was working through an ankle issue during Week 10 prep before being cleared to play, and he'll continue to operate in a rotational role in the backfield behind Gibbs. Through eight regular-season games, Vaki has turned 36 carries into 163 yards (4.5 YPC) and eight catches on nine targets for 81 yards. The Lions will be at home for three of their next four games, starting with Week 11 against the Buccaneers on Nov. 22.

short_comment: Gibbs carried the ball 22 times for 153 yards and two touchdowns while catching seven of eight targets for 99 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots.
long_comment: Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game early for New England, setting the stage for the rout, and Gibbs took full advantage as he set new season highs in receiving yards and scrimmage yards. It's the fourth time in 2026 that the star RB has topped 150 rushing yards, and his fourth game with multiple TDs. Gibbs has amassed 1,384 scrimmage yards and 13 total touchdowns through nine contests as he gets ready to face a stingy Buccaneers run defense in Week 11.

short_comment: Goff completed 20 of 31 passes for 303 yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich. He added three yards on his only carry.
long_comment: A potential barn burner versus Drake Maye never materialized when the New England quarterback left the game early with an ankle injury, but Goff and the Detroit offense still held up their end of the bargain. Two of Goff's TDs went to Amon-Ra St. Brown, including a 56-yard catch-and-run score in the first quarter, while Isaac TeSlaa also hauled in a 12-yard score in the second. Goff will take an 18:4 TD:INT through nine games into a Week 11 clash at home against the Buccaneers.

short_comment: Wonnum (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Patriots in Munich, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.
long_comment: Wonnum entered the league's concussion protocol during the Lions' Week 8 win over the Vikings. He was held out of Detroit's Week 9 win over Miami, but Wonnum has cleared protocol after passing an evaluation by an independent neurologist. His return bolsters the Lions' rotational depth on the defensive line alongside Aidan Hutchinson, Tyler Lacy and Derrick Moore.

short_comment: Branch (hip) was a full participant in practice Thursday.
long_comment: Branch upgraded his practice status to full participation after beginning the week limited. The 25-year-old has 14 tackles (seven solo) and one interception in three regular-season games.

short_comment: Joseph (knee) did not travel to Munich with the Lions and is ruled out for Sunday's matchup against the Patriots.
long_comment: Joseph was a full participant in practice Thursday, but it appears the Lions are taking a cautious approach to his return. The 25-year-old has one more chance to return from the reserve/PUP list in Week 11 before he becomes ineligible for the remainder of the season.

short_comment: Clark registered five tackles (three solo) and one interception during the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins in Week 9.
long_comment: Clark jumped in front of a Malik Willis (abdomen) deep pass intended for Caleb Douglas early in the third quarter, which the Lions offense converted into a 33-yard field goal by Jake Bates eight plays later. It was Clark's second interception of the season and first since Week 1 against the Saints. The veteran safety is up to 49 tackles (28 solo), including 1.0 sacks, three pass defenses and one forced fumble through eight regular-season games.

short_comment: Saylors (neck) was a full participant at practice Wednesday.
long_comment: Saylors sat out his first game of the season in Week 9 due to a neck injury, but it now looks like he's on track to return to game action in Week 10. With teammate Sione Vaki tending to an ankle issue, it appears possible Saylors could be called upon for a larger share of offensive snaps than usual versus the Patriots.

short_comment: The Lions acquired Cisco from the Jets on Monday in exchange for a 2029 sixth-round pick, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
long_comment: Cisco will now suit up for his third NFL team after spending time with the Jaguars and Jets since entering the league in 2021. He had served mainly as a special-teams contributor over his final six games with Jacksonville, but Cisco should see more playing time on defense for a leaky Detroit secondary.

short_comment: The Lions moved Campbell (neck) to injured reserve Saturday.
long_comment: Campbell suffered a neck injury while making a tackle in the third quarter of last Sunday's win over Minnesota and remains in the hospital. Detroit head coach Dan Campbell shared Friday that the linebacker continues to improve, but  his placement on IR means he'll miss at least the team's next four games. K.J. Britt, who Detroit signed off New England's practice squad Wednesday, may be asked to immediately step into a starting role.

short_comment: Rolder (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday.
long_comment: This move was anticipated, as Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury in the Lions' win over Minnesota on Sunday. The rookie linebacker logged a career-high 17 defensive snaps and notched his first NFL sack in that contest, so his injury comes at an unfortunate time. Rolder will now turn his focus toward rehabbing the injury in order to be ready for offseason activities in 2027.

short_comment: McCreary (foot) is active for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
long_comment: McCreary wasn't listed on the injury report Wednesday or Thursday but practiced in a limited capacity Friday. As a result, the 26-year-old was listed as questionable for the divisional showdown with Minnesota, though he has since been cleared to suit up. McCreary has appeared in all six of Detroit's regular-season games in 2026, amassing 22 total tackles (17 solo), 1.0 sacks and one forced fumble.

short_comment: Moore's ankle injury is not considered serious, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: The Packers' decision to rule Moore out with an ankle injury in Week 10 was a precautionary move after the 26-year-old made his first appearance since returning from injured reserve. It's unclear if the fifth-year pro is expected to miss time, but Savion Williams and Matthew Golden will likely act as primary return options if Moore misses time.

short_comment: Head coach Matt LaFleur acknowledged that Parsons (knee/illness) could be ready to make his season debut following the Packers' Week 11 bye, but he still has "a couple more hurdles" to clear before being deemed ready to play, Ryan Wood of USA Today reports.
long_comment: Since opening Parsons' 21-day practice window Nov. 4, the Packers have seemingly targeted their Nov. 25 matchup with the Rams in Week 12 for the star pass rusher's 2026 debut. That plan doesn't appear to have changed while Parsons has been a limited participant in practice for the past two weeks, but he'll likely need to start practicing in full during Week 12 prep before the Packers give him the green light to play. If Parsons does in fact gain clearance to play against the Rams, he could be operating with a restricted snap count in what would mark his first game action since tearing his ACL on Dec. 14, 2025.

short_comment: Taylor completed one of two pass attempts for three yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: Down 20 points with four minutes remaining in the fourth quarter and with starting quarterback Jordan Love having already taken eight sacks on the afternoon, the Packers opted to turn to Taylor to direct the offense for their final possession of the day. All three of Taylor's appearances on the season have now come late in blowout wins or losses, and his opportunities are likely to remain limited to garbage-time situations so long as Love is healthy.

short_comment: Lloyd finished Sunday's loss to Minnesota with 13 yards on four carries while catching all three of his targets for 26 yards.
long_comment: With Josh Jacobs (finger) sidelined, Green Bay turned to the trio of Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Chris Brooks in the backfield. Johnson led the team with 10 carries and 42 total yards despite not getting any targets. Meanwhile, Lloyd turned his seven touches into 39 yards, and Brooks tallied just three yards on his three touches. Green Bay is on bye during the coming week, but Jacobs may still miss the team's next game, which will take place Wednesday, Nov. 25, against the Rams. If that's the case, Lloyd will likely work as part of a shared backfield again, which isn't great for his fantasy outlook.

short_comment: Johnson carried the ball 10 times for 42 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: The former Steeler led the Packers' backfield in totes and rushing yards, with MarShawn Lloyd chipping in 39 scrimmage yards on seven touches. Johnson has produced modest but decent numbers over the last two games, averaging a 4.6 YPC on 24 carries as the top early-down option for Green Bay. Josh Jacobs (finger) could return after the team's Week 11 bye, but if he isn't cleared, Johnson could find himself atop the depth chart again in Week 12 against the Rams.

short_comment: Kraft caught one of four targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: The tight end's numbers reflected how much time his quarterback had to look downfield, as Jordan Love got sacked eight times in the rout. Kraft has been held to just one catch in back-to-back games, and he heads into a Week 11 bye with a 37-370-3 line on 56 targets through 10 games, with the Rams as the next opponent on the horizon in Week 12.

short_comment: Golden caught five of nine targets for 70 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: The second-year wideout was the only Packer to have much success on offense, leading the team in catches, targets and receiving yards. Golden has reached 70 yards in three straight games and five of the last six, and he heads into a Week 11 bye with a 58-853-5 line on 101 targets through 10 contests. His next chance to add to those numbers will come in Week 12 against the Rams.

short_comment: Watson caught three of five targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to Minnesota.
long_comment: The Packers' passing game was stifled as the Vikings sacked Jordan Love eight times, giving him little time to find receivers like Watson. The 37 yards were a season low for the fifth-year wideout, while the three grabs tied for his lowest volume of 2026. Watson will take a 52-916-7 line on 79 targets through 10 contests into a Week 11 bye before facing the Rams in Week 12.

short_comment: Love completed 17 of 27 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: The 28-year-old QB came into the game having been sacked just 17 times in his first nine games of the season, but Minnesota brought Love down eight times Sunday. Despite that onslaught, he was able to find J. Michael Sturdivant for a 32-yard TD in the third quarter to salvage his line slightly. It was the first time since Week 6 that Love had failed to throw multiple touchdowns, and just the second time all season. He'll get a Week 11 bye to heal up from Sunday's pummeling before facing Myles Garrett and the Rams in Week 12.

short_comment: Melton (thigh) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Vikings, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Melton exited Sunday's game because of a thigh injury, and he will not be cleared to return to the contest. Skyy Moore (ankle) will also not return, so Savion Williams and Matthew Golden will operate as the top return options on kickoffs and punts.

short_comment: Cisse (ribs) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Vikings.
long_comment: Cisse picked up the injury during the first quarter, and he's being checked on by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's game. Carrington Valentine, Kamal Hadden and Benjamin St-Juste are candidates for more defensive snaps while Cisse is being evaluated in the locker room.

short_comment: Glover (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
long_comment: Glover's practice reps were limited during Week 10 prep due to a knee injury that prevented him from playing against the Patriots in Week 9. The third-year pro was cleared by medical staff to play Sunday, and he should reclaim his starting role at right guard from Laken Tomlinson.

short_comment: Van Ness (back) is active for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
long_comment: Van Ness upgraded to limited in Friday's practice while dealing with a back injury. The weakside linebacker has recovered enough to suit up for Sunday's contest against a Vikings team that is also fighting for the NFC North title.

short_comment: Bullard (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
long_comment: Bullard was upgraded to a limited participant in Friday's practice and is questionable ahead of Sunday's contest. The starting slot cornerback is all set to suit up, seemingly having overcome his ankle injury in time for a heavyweight NFC North bout with the Vikings.

short_comment: McKinney (foot) is active for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
long_comment: McKinney sustained a foot injury during Friday's practice session. Despite the late-week injury, the star free safety is all set to suit up for Sunday's divisional contest. McKinney enters Week 10 with five interceptions, tying Amani Hooker for the league lead.

short_comment: Brooks (ankle) is active for Sunday's game versus the Vikings, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
long_comment: Brooks is back after a five-game stint on injured reserve due to an ankle issue that he suffered in Week 4. With top RB Josh Jacobs (finger) out of the lineup and Pierre Strong a healthy scratch Sunday, Brooks rejoins a backfield composed of MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson. Brooks got some modest run with the Packers offense before he was sidelined, turning 15 rushes into 70 yards (4.7 YPC) and three catches (on five targets) for 24 yards, but he's most valuable in pass protection for QB Jordan Love.

short_comment: The Packers elevated Dabney from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday.
long_comment: It's the second straight week Dabney has been elevated. He didn't get any snaps on offense last Sunday against New England but did play six snaps on special teams. Josh Whyle (concussion) was placed on IR on Saturday, so Dabney is set to take Whyle's role as a depth tight end and contributor on special teams.

short_comment: Green Bay placed Whyle (concussion) on injured reserve Saturday.
long_comment: Whyle suffered a concussion in Week 8 against Carolina and missed last Sunday's win over the Patriots. He had already been ruled for Sunday's contest against Minnesota before the Packers decided to place him on IR. Whyle didn't log a catch or target during his eight contests before getting hurt, so his blocking and work on special teams will be the primary voids during his absence.

short_comment: Banks (knee/hip) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
long_comment: Banks' practice reps were limited while managing knee and hip injuries. However, the sixth-year pro has been cleared to play Sunday, and he'll continue to serve as the Packers' starter at left guard.

short_comment: Schultz caught one pass for an 11-yard touchdown on two targets in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns.
long_comment: While Schultz got into the end zone for the first time this campaign, his catches and targets were new single-game lows for 2026. Schultz has yet to produce more than 45 yards in a game when Nico Collins is healthy this season. The veteran tight end is a low-floor, TD-or-bust fantasy bet.

short_comment: Demercado rushed seven times for 16 yards and brought in one of two targets for minus-1 yard in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
long_comment: Demercado opened the game as a reserve in his second appearance in a Texans uniform, but Woody Marks' third-quarter exit due to a concussion left the former in the de facto No. 1 role. That still didn't lead to much opportunity for Demercado in a game during which Houston squandered a 17-0 first-half lead. However, DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN.com reports Marks is unlikely to play in Week 11 due to the short turnaround for a home matchup against the Colts, meaning Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale could have expanded roles in that game unless David Montgomery (groin) is able to suit up.

short_comment: Dell brought in three of four targets for 21 yards and rushed once for no gain in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
long_comment: One week after posting a 105-yard effort against the Chargers in only his second game since 2024, Dell saw a big downturn in yardage Sunday. Nevertheless, the fact he retained a solid complementary role was encouraging, and the speedy wideout seems to be playing unencumbered by any physical or mental limitations following the recovery from his devastating knee injury. Dell will look to boost his yardage back up in a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Colts on Thursday night.

short_comment: Hutchinson brought in four of nine targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
long_comment: Hutchinson, who was checked for a concussion during the fourth quarter, finished second across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets for the Texans. He also recorded a touchdown grab for the third straight game on an 11-yard catch early in the second quarter, and his receiving yardage tally was his highest since Week 5. Hutchinson now sports a 28-345-3 receiving line on 54 targets as he continues to function in a steady complementary role heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Colts on Thursday night.

short_comment: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Sunday that he's "not certain" if Montgomery (groin) will be able to play Thursday against Indianapolis, DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN reports.
long_comment: Montgomery hasn't suited up since he suffered a groin injury Week 5 in Tennessee. However, he practiced in full this past Friday for the first time since getting hurt, and the Texans described his work during Week 10 prep as a "ramp-up" ahead of potentially returning Week 11. Ryans didn't sound certain after Sunday's loss to Cleveland that Montgomery will be able to play versus the Colts, but if the veteran running back does suit up, it could be a huge boost to a Houston offense that may be without the RB who has been filling in as the starter for Montgomery. Woody Marks suffered a concussion Sunday and isn't likely to be cleared in time to play Thursday.

short_comment: Stroud completed 20 of 38 passes for 211 yards with three touchdowns and one interception while adding three rushes for 20 yards in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
long_comment: Stroud looked like he was on his way to another highly productive day early while helping stake the Texans to a 17-0 lead in the first half, but the fourth-year signal-caller and his offense largely stagnated in the second half. Stroud spread the ball around while connecting with eight different targets overall, and his trio of scoring strikes went to Nico Collins (12 yards), Xavier Hutchinson (11 yards) and Dalton Schultz (11 yards), the latter accounting for Houston's only second-half points. Despite the Texans' monumental collapse, Stroud's highly impressive season continues, as he's up to 2,462 passing yards, a 19:3 TD:INT and 120 rushing yards and another score heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Colts on Thursday night.

short_comment: Coach DeMeco Ryans acknowledged after Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns that Marks (concussion) is unlikely to play in Thursday night's game against the Colts, ESPN.com's DJ Bien-Aime reports.
long_comment: With the Texans on a short week ahead of the contest, Ryans noted of Marks, "Just not enough time for him to turn it around that quickly." As for the Week 11 status of fellow RB David Montgomery (groin) -- who was inactive again Sunday -- Ryans said, "I'm not certain if David can play or not," adding "We'll take it one day at a time to see how he feels and how he can get back." Prior to his exit Sunday, Marks had 12 carries for 50 yards and one catch for 15 yards. Meanwhile, Emari Demercado finished with seven carries for 16 yards and one catch for minus-one yard, while Dare Ogunbowale logged one carry for two yards and one catch for 13 yards.

short_comment: Collins secured nine of 16 targets for 94 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
long_comment: Collins comfortably paced the Texans across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and he added his fifth touchdown of the season on a 12-yard catch in the first quarter. Collins also had a 16-yard reception on Houston's last-gasp drive wiped out by an offensive holding penalty, but he still finished with season highs in receptions and targets. Collins retains an unquestioned No. 1 role in the Texans' prolific air attack, affording him an enticing combination of floor and upside heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Colts on Thursday night.

short_comment: Hummel (groin) is active  for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
long_comment: Hummel is set to play in his first contest since the Texans' Week 1 loss to the Bills, when the linebacker sustained an ankle injury. The 27-year-old was activated from injured reserve on Nov. 14 and is set to return to his reserve role for the team's defense and special teams in Week 10.

short_comment: Smith (illness) is active for Sunday's game against the Browns.
long_comment: Smith has recovered from Friday's illness enough to suit up for Sunday's contest. The reserve offensive tackle is one of the primary depth options behind starters Trent Brown and Aireontae Ersery.

short_comment: Anderson (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Browns.
long_comment: The Texans' star pass rusher is all set to suit up for Sunday's showdown. Anderson has 9.5 sacks through eight games, entering Week 10 as the league leader. The Defensive Player of the Year candidate will look to continue to pressure his opponents after recovering from an ankle injury he sustained in Week 9 against the Chargers.

short_comment: The Texans signed Ogunbowale to the practice squad and elevated him to the active roster Saturday.
long_comment: Ogunbowale was released by the Texans on Thursday after appearing in each of the team's five prior games. He's opted to stay in Houston as a member of the practice squad, and his elevation to the 53-man roster comes after David Montgomery (groin) was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns. Ogunbowale and Emari Demercado will provide depth for the Texans behind lead back Woody Marks in Week 10.

short_comment: Blankenship (concussion/hand) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Browns.
long_comment: Blankenship ended Week 10 prep with back-to-back full practices, and he's progressed enough through the league's concussion protocol to be cleared to play Sunday. He is also working through a left hand injury that required surgery in October, but that won't prevent him from playing against Cleveland. Blankenship's return means M.J. Stewart will revert to a rotational role in the secondary.

short_comment: The Texans claimed Remigio off waivers from the Chiefs on Thursday.
long_comment: Remigio appeared in each of the Chiefs' first eight games of the regular season before being cut by the team Tuesday. He predominantly served on special teams as a returner on kickoffs and punts with Kansas City, and he figures to reprise that role in Houston, although he'll be competing for that role with Tremon Smith, Tank Dell, Woody Marks and Xavier Hutchinson.

short_comment: The Texans designated Smith (hamstring) to return from injured reserve Wednesday.
long_comment: Smith landed on injured reserve in early October due to a hamstring injury. He's progressed enough in his recovery to return to practice and was a limited participant in Wednesday's session. Smith would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Browns.

short_comment: Mills completed one of two pass attempts for seven yards and lost two yards on two carries in Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers.
long_comment: Since the Texans had built their lead to 19 with less than five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, head coach DeMeco Ryans opted to pull starting quarterback C.J. Stroud from the game and handed the offense over to Mills. In what marked his first playing time of the season, Mills directed two possessions. He led the Texans to a field goal with 2:20 remaining, then knelt twice to run out the clock when Houston got the ball back with 1:07 left. With Stroud enjoying a bounce-back campaign, Mills' opportunities will likely be limited to garbage-time situations if Stroud stays healthy.

short_comment: Stover was a healthy inactive for Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers.
long_comment: Week 9 marked the first time all season that Stover sat out, with the Texans opting to keep their other four tight ends (Dalton Schultz, Foster Moreau, Brevin Jordan and Marlin Klein) active ahead of him. Through the Texans' first seven games, Stover had played less than half of the offensive snaps in each contest and recorded three receptions for 17 yards on five targets while rushing three times for five yards.

short_comment: Moreau didn't log any targets or touches Sunday in a 44-22 win against the Chargers.
long_comment: For the second straight week, Moreau didn't make a mark in the box score. He did technically draw a target (which he didn't catch), but it was wiped out by an accepted defensive penalty. Moreau hasn't had more than two catches in any game this season and has finished with fewer than 10 yards in every contest since Week 3, so he's not a viable fantasy play in virtually any format right now.

short_comment: Colts head coach Shane Steichen reported Ward (shin) didn't return to Sunday's 24-22 win over the Dolphins and could miss Thursday's game versus Houston, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Not only was Ward injured in Week 10, but Sauce Gardner (calf) was also ruled out before the end of the contest. With both Ward and Gardner in danger of missing Thursday's game against the Texans, Kenneth Harris and Kapena Gushiken could be in line for more snaps alongside Justin Walley.

short_comment: McGowan rushed 12 times for 77 yards and a touchdown and returned two kickoffs for 61 yards in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
long_comment: The rookie had shown well in recent weeks while trade speculation swirled around Jonathan Taylor, and even though the latter ultimately stayed put at the deadline, McGowan still compiled a new career high in rush attempts and rushing yards. The Kentucky product also followed up his first career rushing touchdown in Week 9 against the Cowboys with a four-yard scoring run early in the second quarter Sunday, and McGowan was also productive in his returner role. While Taylor should remain the de facto top backfield option for the Colts, McGowan should remain in an elevated role for what remains of Indianapolis' non-contending season.

short_comment: Jones completed 11 of 22 passes for 108 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions while adding five carries for nine yards in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.
long_comment: Jones failed to eclipse the 200-yard mark for the fourth straight game while throwing multiple picks for the second time in that span. Neither turnover led to any Dolphins points, and Jones also threw a seven-yard touchdown pass to new interim No. 1 receiver Laquon Treadwell in the second quarter. Jones has completed just 59.6 percent of his passes and has a 7:12 TD:INT across 10 games, and with Indianapolis devoid of any realistic postseason aspirations, it may not be long before Anthony Richardson is given an opportunity under center. However, Joel A. Erickson of The Indy Star reports that head coach Shane Steichen has already named Jones the starter for Thursday's Week 11 road matchup against the Texans.

short_comment: Warren rushed once for three yards and brought in two of three targets for one yard in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
long_comment: The new-look Colts offense was without Josh Downs and Keenan Allen after trade-deadline moves, but Warren was still surprisingly uninvolved. Daniel Jones completed only 50.0 percent of his passes and threw for just 108 yards, however, so Warren's minimal production is somewhat understandable in that context. Jones has thrown for under 200 yards in four consecutive games and is playing generally uninspired football, so Warren's fantasy outlook remains shaky for the time being but could improve if Anthony Richardson takes over under center at some point.

short_comment: Taylor rushed 16 times for 83 yards and brought in two of four targets for 20 yards in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that stayed with Indianapolis.
long_comment: Taylor made it through the trade deadline unscathed after rumors swirled around a possible change of scenery, but the talented back still split plenty of work with rookie backfield mate Seth McGowan, who logged 12 carries. Taylor still remained the No. 1 option and was the only one of the two to see any targets, and the rushing yardage total was his best since Week 7, just before serious trade speculation began. Taylor is staying put for the rest of the campaign, but it seems likely that he'll continue ceding a fair share of touches to McGowan moving forward.

short_comment: Raimann has entered the league's concussion protocol and has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Dolphins, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Raimann took a hit to the head in the first quarter, and following tests by medical staff, the fifth-year offensive lineman has been diagnosed with a concussion. Luke Tenuta will stay in at left tackle for the rest of Sunday's game due to the absence of Raimann, who faces an uphill battle to play in the Colts' Week 11 tilt against the Texans on Thursday Night Football.

short_comment: The Colts elevated Watkins from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
long_comment: The move gives the Colts more depth at wide receiver after the team traded Josh Downs and Keenan Allen to the Chiefs and 49ers, respectively, on Thursday. If Watkins sees the field against the Dolphins on Sunday, then it would mark his first regular-season appearance since 2023 as a member of the Eagles, when he appeared in nine regular-season games and accumulated 15 catches (on 21 targets) for 142 yards and a touchdown.

short_comment: The Colts placed Davis-Gaither (knee) on injured reserve Saturday.
long_comment: Davis-Gaither was already ruled out for Sunday's game against Miami in what would be his second consecutive missed contest due to a knee injury. Now that he's been placed on IR, the seventh-year pro will be required to miss at least four games, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Titans on Sunday, Dec. 20.

short_comment: Key (hamstring) was activated from injured reserve Saturday and does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
long_comment: Key missed the Colts' last five games while on injured reserve due to a hamstring injury that he sustained in Week 4 against the Commanders. He was cleared to return to practice Wednesday and logged a trio of full sessions, which gave the Colts the confidence to activate the veteran defensive lineman from IR ahead of Sunday's contest. Prior to his IR stint, Key posted eight tackles (three solo), including 0.5 sacks, and one forced fumble in four regular-season games.

short_comment: The Colts placed Alie-Cox (groin) on injured reserve Saturday.
long_comment: Alie-Cox was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, and his groin injury is severe enough for him to warrant a stint on injured reserve. That means he'll be required to miss at least four games, and with the Colts on a bye for Week 13, that means the next time Alie-Cox can play is Week 15 against the Titans on Sunday, Dec. 20. Will Mallory (hamstring) has also been ruled out for Week 10, so Drew Ogletree and Pharaoh Brown will serve as the Colts' backup tight ends behind Tyler Warren against Miami.

short_comment: Haulcy (ankle) was a full participant at Thursday's practice.
long_comment: Haulcy missed the Colts' Week 9 loss to Dallas due to an ankle injury and sat out practice Wednesday, but his return without limitations Thursday suggests the rookie third-round pick is ready to return to action. He's poised to reclaim the starting strong safety role Sunday against the Dolphins.

short_comment: Allen recorded 10 tackles (three solo) and a pass breakup in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.
long_comment: With Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee) out versus Dallas, Allen played all 79 defensive snaps for Indy, marking the first time the second-round rookie has played 100 percent of the defensive snaps in a game. He's started back-to-back contests and is up to 25 tackles (nine solo), including 1.0 sacks, and the one pass breakup across six appearances this season.

short_comment: Boettcher recorded 12 tackles (four solo) in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.
long_comment: With Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee) inactive against Dallas, Boettcher saw a spike in playing time alongside CJ Allen at linebacker for the Colts. The fourth-round rookie Boettcher played a season-high 73 percent of the defensive snaps and recorded his first career game with double-digit tackles.

short_comment: Wohler recorded 16 tackles (six solo) in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.
long_comment: With A.J. Haulcy (ankle) inactive, Wohler made the spot start alongside Cam Bynum at safety for the Colts. Wohler played 98 percent of the defensive snaps against Dallas, easily a new career-high playing-time clip for the second-year safety after he missed his entire rookie season with a foot injury. Once Haulcy returns, Wohler will likely return to a reserve and special-teams role.

short_comment: Walley (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
long_comment: After being injured in Week 7, Walley has missed the past two games but appears ready to return to the lineup Sunday against the Dolphins. He's spent most of his time covering the slot for the Colts this season, recording 35 tackles (23 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and three pass breakups across seven appearances.

short_comment: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Wednesday that Burks and Anthony Gould will step into larger roles after the team traded Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: A rookie seventh-round pick with 4.30 speed, Burks has caught six of nine targets for 60 yards across 49 routes (18.3 percent target rate, 1.22 yards per route). He won't necessarily see a lot of targets in an offense that runs through the RBs and TEs, but Burks should at least get far more playing time in the second half of the season, if only because the Colts' other wideouts are veterans with minimal history of production. Laquon Treadwell and Ashton Dulin are the other favorites for regular playing time, and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine is also on the roster.

short_comment: When asked Wednesday whether Pierce (heel) has a chance to return from IR this season, Colts head coach Shane Steichen was noncommittal, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: "We'll see. Like I said last week, he's still in that rehab process, and I'm not going to put a timetable on return," Steichen noted of the wideout, who's been on IR since Sept. 26. At 2-7, the Colts were sellers ahead of the NFL's trade deadline, so the team presumably has no reason rush Pierce back. With Keenan Allen and Josh Downs no longer in the mix, Indy's healthy WRs for now are Ashton Dulin, Laquon Treadwell, Anthony Gould, Deion Burks and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine.

short_comment: Allen went without a carry or target while playing 12 of the Jaguars' 73 offensive snaps in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
long_comment: As a rookie seventh-round pick last season, Allen carved out a fairly consistent role as a third-down specialist, but he's struggled to earn the same level of playing time in Year 2. With Bhayshul Tuten earning more trust on passing downs and with Chris Rodriguez and Ameer Abdullah also on hand as complementary options, Allen hasn't topped a 20 percent snap share in any of the Jaguars' first nine games. Altogether, Allen has logged just one carry (for one yard) to go with two receptions for nine yards on eight targets.

short_comment: Rodriguez rushed for five yards on four carries in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
long_comment: Rodriguez was out-carried 26 to four by Bhayshul Tuten, who has very much proven himself as the Jaguars' clear RB1 in one of the league's best offenses. Tuten also out-snapped Rodriguez 52 to 10, while LeQuint Allen (12 snaps) saw more playing time. Rodriguez is little more than a deep-league bench stash should something happen to Tuten.

short_comment: Cameron caught all three of his targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23, Week 10 win over Tennessee. He also returned five kickoffs for 142 yards.
long_comment: Cameron gave the Jaguars a 14-point lead early in the fourth quarter when he hauled in a 25-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence. It was the rookie wideout's third touchdown of the campaign but his first since Week 3. Cameron's 67 receiving yards marked a career high, while his three receptions tied the most he's had as a pro. Cameron's propensity for finding the end zone (his three TDs have come on just 12 total catches) is appealing, but at this point he isn't getting enough volume to be a reliable week-to-week fantasy asset.

short_comment: Thomas caught three of four targets for 29 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
long_comment: The three catches tied his season high, while the four targets represented his biggest volume since Week 2. The Jaguars' decision not to deal Thomas at the trade deadline remains a curious one, as the third-year wideout simply doesn't have a significant role in Liam Coen's offense and might not step into one even if someone like Parker Washington got injured -- Josh Cameron was more productive Sunday on three targets and caught one of Trevor Lawrence's three TDs. Thomas will take a 13-146-2 line on 26 targets over nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

short_comment: Meyers caught three of six targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
long_comment: The six targets were second on the Jaguars behind Parker Washington's nine, but Meyers' longest gain of the day went for only 15 yards. The veteran wideout has also failed to find the end zone in six straight games, a stretch in which he's managed just a 19-256-0 line on 32 targets. Meyers will try to end that drought in a Week 11 clash against the Giants.

short_comment: Washington caught seven of nine targets for 152 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
long_comment: The 152 receiving yards were a new career high for Washington, and the fourth-year WR highlighted his big day with a two-yard TD toss from Trevor Lawrence in the first quarter to open the scoring. It's Washington's second game this season with 100-plus yards, and he'll take a 36-645-6 line on 64 targets through nine contests into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

short_comment: Tuten carried the ball 26 times for 88 yards and a touchdown and caught three of four targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over Tennessee.
long_comment: It's the second time this season that Tuten has reached triple-digit scrimmage yards in a game, with both those performances coming since the Jaguars' Week 7 bye. The second-year RB capped the rout with a six-yard TD run in the fourth quarter, extending his scoring streak to four games -- a stretch in which Tuten has racked up 260 rushing yards and three touchdowns on the ground while adding a 9-128-3 line on 10 targets through the air. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 11 against the Giants.

short_comment: Lawrence completed 25 of 35 passes for 352 yards and three touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. He added 27 yards on four carries.
long_comment: It was another huge performance from the 27-year-old QB, as Lawrence set a new season high in passing yards and threw at least three TDs for the fifth time in nine games to begin the year. He spread the ball around again, as seven different Jaguars caught multiple passes and Parker Washington, Josh Cameron and Brenton Strange were all on the other end of scores. Lawrence will take a sharp 21:5 TD:INT into a Week 11 clash with the Giants.

short_comment: Strange caught two of three targets for nine yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
long_comment: The Jaguars keep blowing out their opponents, and Strange contributed a three-yard touchdown Sunday but was otherwise not heard from much, as Parker Washington dog-walked the Titans' secondary for 7-152-1 receiving on nine targets. Strange's touchdown grab was his first since Week 1. He remans a locked-in TE1 for fantasy, as he is playing virtually every snap in an elite offense.

short_comment: Hainsey (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Titans.
long_comment: Hainsey appeared to injure his knee while blocking on a run play in the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's contest. Jonah Monheim has taken over at center in Hainsey's absence.

short_comment: Striggow is being evaluated for a possible concussion and is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Titans.
long_comment: Striggow has operated in a rotational role on the defensive line, so Bryan Thomas should see a bump in defensive snaps for as long as the former is out of the game.

short_comment: Green (forearm) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Green's 21-day practice window opened Nov. 11. The Jaguars' defensive end logged three consecutive full sessions in his return to practice but was ultimately deemed not ready to suit up for Week 10.

short_comment: Walker (ribs) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Walker played through a rib injury during the Jaguars' win over the Ravens in Week 9. The defensive end sat out Wednesday's practice session to nurse the issue before logging consecutive limited practices to end Week 10 prep. Walker is set to once again play through the nagging injury in Sunday's divisional showdown with the Titans.

short_comment: The Jaguars acquired Godchaux from the Saints on Monday in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick, though the selection could turn into a 2027 sixth-round pick if "conditions are met," Jonathan Jones of The Athletic of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Godchaux was selected by Miami in the fifth round of the 2017 NFL Draft. Since then, he has appeared in 145 regular-season games for the Dolphins, Patriots and Saints, garnering 487 total tackles (224 solo), 5.5 sacks and three forced fumbles. Godchaux's presence will bolster depth at the defensive tackle position for the Jaguars, especially with DaVon Hamilton (knee) done for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

short_comment: Oluokun recorded seven tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, in Thursday's 33-10 victory over Baltimore.
long_comment: Oluokun tied for his team's lead in stops and notched his second sack of the season when he brought down Joe Fagnano early in the second quarter. Oluokun has been a reliable fantasy IDP asset in 2026 with at least seven tackles in six of his eight games so far. He's tallied 58 total stops, including the 2.0 sacks, along with two interceptions and a forced fumble.

short_comment: Koziol finished Thursday's 33-10 win over Baltimore with two catches for 15 yards on two targets.
long_comment: Koziol was part of a three-tight-end starting unit for Jacksonville alongside Brenton Strange and Nate Boerkircher. Koziol logged the fewest offensive snaps (12) among the trio but matched both in receptions. He entered Thursday with just one catch through five contests, so it's probably not wise to count on him for substantial production moving forward.

short_comment: Armstrong caught his only target for a 43-yard touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
long_comment: The wideout played just 17 of 64 offensive snaps against Atlanta and ran only seven pass routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks. Armstrong was tasked with blocking duties on 10 of his snaps. He still managed to catch his first career touchdown in the fourth quarter with the game already well out of hand. Armstrong is not on the fantasy radar.

short_comment: Allen caught two of four targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
long_comment: The rookie wideout scored his first career touchdown by beating the cornerback on a stutter-go for a 39-yard touchdown in the third quarter. With Josh Downs still getting comfortable and learning the offense following Tuesday's acquisition from the Colts, Allen maintained a significant role on offense, playing 22 of 64 offensive snaps. Once Downs progresses from the 10 snaps he played against Atlanta, it will be interesting to see if Allen can push Xavier Worthy (zero catches on three targets across 56 snaps on Sunday) for a larger piece of the outside receiver role in Kansas City's offense.

short_comment: Worthy failed to catch any of his three targets in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
long_comment: Worthy ran a team-high 37 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks, but on a day Mahomes targeted nine different players, Worthy was the only one to not record a catch. With Josh Downs now in the fold and working to get comfortable in the offense, Worthy's role will likely only continue to shrink. On just eight routes in his team debut Sunday, Downs posted a 4-53-1 receiving line on five targets. Worthy hasn't produced that many fantasy points in a game all season. He's waiver-wire fodder in 12-team redraft leagues.

short_comment: Kelce secured both targets for 30 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
long_comment: Kelce recorded a 23-yard catch on the Chiefs' first play from scrimmage, seemingly a harbinger of a productive day. However, the veteran tight end also suffered an ankle injury on the tackle, and although he was able to return to the game, he had only one more reception the rest of the way. Despite the modest numbers, Kelce managed to keep his season-long streak of games with multiple receptions going, and he's averaging a career-best 14.6  per catch heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

short_comment: Downs secured four of five targets for 53 yards and a touchdown, fumbled once but recovered and returned three punts for 10 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
long_comment: Making his Chiefs debut following three days of practice after arriving via trade from the Colts on Tuesday, Downs looked right at home in the Patrick Mahomes-led offense. The young wideout fully capitalized on the upgrade he saw at quarterback, finishing third in receptions, receiving yards and targets right out of the gate and adding his second touchdown of the season on a difficult 18-yard catch just before halftime. Downs' immediate chemistry with Mahomes is highly welcome news for fantasy managers, and he'll aim to carry the momentum over into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

short_comment: Johnson rushed 22 times for 101 yards and brought in six of seven targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
long_comment: Drawing his first career start due to Kenneth Walker (groin) being sidelined, Johnson put on a pretty convincing impression of his star teammate. Not only did Johnson just get himself over the century mark in rushing yards, but he finished as the team leader in receptions and targets while checking in as the runner-up in receiving yards. Johnson struck from 12 and six yards out for his two receiving TDs, underscoring his considerable versatility. If Walker is unable to garner active status for next Sunday's Week 11 matchup against the Cardinals, the Chiefs' ground attack will remain in good hands with Johnson.

short_comment: Rice brought in five of six targets for 82 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
long_comment: Rice led the Chiefs in receiving yards and finished second in receptions and targets on a prolific afternoon for the Chiefs' air attack. Rice didn't get in on the scoring fun of a five-touchdown day for Patrick Mahomes, but he still eclipsed 80 receiving yards for the third time this season and first time since Week 3. Rice's level of involvement was encouraging given the debuting Josh Downs drew five targets, keeping the former's prospects bright for a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

short_comment: Mahomes completed 22 of 35 passes for 348 yards with five touchdowns and no interceptions while adding two rushes for 15 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
long_comment: Taking advantage of a controlled environment and a fast track at Mercedes-Benz Stadium -- not to mention the presence of the debuting Josh Downs -- Mahomes repeatedly exploited the vulnerabilities of the Falcons defense throughout the afternoon. The legendary signal-caller showed no ill effects from the elbow injury that he'd suffered in Week 9, and he connected with Emmett Johnson (12, six yards), Downs (18 yards), Cyrus Allen (39 yards) and Andrew Armstrong (43 yards) for his quintet of touchdown passes. Mahomes now has multiple scoring strikes and zero interceptions in three straight games, and Sunday's five TD tosses represented a new season high. Mahomes will take 2,385 passing yards and a 19:4 TD:INT into a Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

short_comment: Wiley suffered a fractured ankle in the Chiefs' 35-13 victory over the Falcons on Sunday, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports.
long_comment: Wiley was carted to the locker room in the first quarter with an ankle injury. The tight end fractured his ankle and did not return to the contest. The 26-year-old will likely be placed on injured reserve soon, as he begins to recover from the injury.

short_comment: Smith (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Falcons.
long_comment: Smith has entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will not return to Sunday's game. Mike Caliendo is set to finish the game at right guard.

short_comment: Delane (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site reports.
long_comment: Delane has been given the green light to return from a two-game absence due to a shoulder injury. The rookie first-rounder will likely return to his starting role at outside cornerback opposite Nohl Williams, while Kristian Fulton and Christian Roland-Wallace provide depth at the position.

short_comment: The Chiefs elevated De Jesus from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
long_comment: It's the first time this season that De Jesus has been elevated to the active roster, and he could make his NFL regular-season debut against the Falcons on Sunday. He signed with the Chiefs in early May as an undrafted free agent out of California, and he joined the team's practice squad Nov. 4 after failing to make the 53-man roster at the end of training camp in late August.

short_comment: The Chiefs elevated Carter from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
long_comment: With Kenneth Walker (groin) ruled out and Jaydn Ott (hamstring) listed as questionable, the elevation of Carter gives the Chiefs additional depth in the backfield behind rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson for Sunday's game against the Falcons. If he sees action, it will be Carter's first appearance of the regular season, and he'll face the team that he suited up for in 2025, when he logged nine carries for 60 yards across seven regular-season contests.

short_comment: Jones recorded four tackles (two solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a pass breakup in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
long_comment: The 32-year-old defensive lineman had gotten off to a slow start to begin the 2026 season, his 11th in the league. Prior to Sunday, he'd recorded just 0.5 sacks across the first seven games, so his 2.0 sacks were his first full ones of the campaign. Jones is now up to 17 tackles (eight solo), including 2.5 sacks, three pass breakups and a fumble recovery on 72 percent of the defensive snaps.

short_comment: Karlaftis recorded six tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a pass breakup in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
long_comment: After starting the season without a sack in his first four games, Karlaftis has 4.0 sacks over his last four contests. For the season, the 25-year-old edge rusher is up to 32 tackles (16 solo), including the 4.0 sacks, a career-high nine pass breakups, including his first career interception, and a forced fumble across eight games. He's on pace to shatter his previous career high of 48 tackles, which was set last season.

short_comment: Bolton recorded 12 tackles (five solo) and a forced fumble in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
long_comment: Bolton doesn't do much in the box scores other than rack up tackles, but he's good at that and now has five double-digit tackles games through eight contests to begin the 2026 campaign. For the season, Bolton is up to 80 tackles (39 solo), two pass breakups and a forced fumble on 99 percent of the Chiefs' defensive snaps.

short_comment: Tranquill collected 13 tackles (seven solo) in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
long_comment: It was Tranquill's second double-digit tackles game of the season, and both have come over the last three weeks. The veteran linebacker has piled up 66 tackles (33 solo), two pass breakups and one fumble recovery on 88 percent of the defensive snaps across eight games this season.

short_comment: Butker will remain Kansas City's kicker ahead of Sunday's game against the Falcons, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports.
long_comment: On that topic, coach Andy Reid said Wednesday, "I'm gonna stick with Butker this week." While the veteran kicker has held on to the top job through the Chiefs' first eight games, he's had accuracy issues this season, having converted 12 of his 19 field-goal attempts and making 22 of his 23 extra-point tries in that span. Reid's comment about Butker on Wednesday implies that the team's kicking situation is being evaluated on a weekly basis. Justin Tucker is on Kansas City's practice squad, and he remains an option should Reid decide that a switch is in order down the road.

short_comment: Young went without a target while playing one of the Raiders' 59 snaps on offense in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks. He also brought back one kickoff for 29 yards.
long_comment: Young has suited up in each of the Raiders' 10 games this season, but he's been deployed almost exclusively on special teams. He's seen single-digit snaps on offense in five straight games and has posted a collective 2-36-0 receiving line on three targets on the campaign.

short_comment: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak confirmed Monday that Bowers (ankle) is considered day-to-day after exiting Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports. "It's not as bad as we thought, but still a significant injury," Kubiak said.
long_comment: Bowers checked in and out of Sunday's contest as he managed the ankle issue, finishing with two catches for 18 yards on two targets while logging just 11 snaps on offense. Per Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com, Kubiak added that Bowers will continue to be evaluated throughout the week as the Raiders look to determine whether the star tight end will be available for next Sunday's game in Denver. If Bowers is forced to miss his third game of the season, the Raiders would have more targets up for grabs for the likes of tight end Michael Mayer, running back Ashton Jeanty and wideouts Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech.

short_comment: Nailor recorded one reception for minus-1 yard on four targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
long_comment: Making his first NFL start, No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza was under siege throughout the afternoon, as a ferocious Seahawks defense sacked him six times and limited him to just 143 passing yards on 29 attempts. As a result, Nailor and the Raiders' other pass catchers were held quiet, with running back Ashton Jeanty (four receptions for 46 yards) being the only Las Vegas player to top two catches and 25 receiving yards. Though Mendoza will get some more favorable matchups over the Raiders' final seven games, Nailor will be difficult to count on for production. Even while Kirk Cousins served as the starting quarterback for Las Vegas before being traded to the Vikings last week, Nailor was limited to just 14 receptions for 122 yards and one touchdown on 28 targets through eight appearances.

short_comment: Laube played all 22 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks and returned two kickoffs for 46 yards and one punt for zero yards.
long_comment: Since earning seven touches in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Patriots, Laube has been an afterthought on offense. He's played just eight total offense snaps in the Raiders' ensuing five games, and Sunday marked the first time all season that he was limited exclusively to special teams.

short_comment: Mayer caught two of three targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
long_comment: Jack Bech (seven targets) was the only Las Vegas player to see more than four targets in Fernando Mendoza's first career start. The rookie quarterback targeted 10 different players on his 29 attempts. With Kirk Cousins' efficiency off to Minnesota, Mayer is a low-floor TE2 for fantasy, but he could get a bit of a boost if Brock Bowers' ankle injury causes him to miss time.

short_comment: Tucker caught one pass for nine yards on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
long_comment: In Fernando Mendoza's first career start at quarterback, Tucker saw just 6.9 percent of the targets, while Jack Bech led the team with seven looks. Tucker looks like someone who won't be usable in fantasy until he shows some tangible chemistry with the young quarterback.

short_comment: Mendoza completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed six times for 22 yards and one TD during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
long_comment: The Mendoza era in Las Vegas officially kicked off this week following the trade of veteran QB Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, and the rookie first overall pick unsurprisingly flashed at times while also stalling numerous drives by taking six sacks overall. On a positive note, Mendoza didn't turn the ball over, and he also recorded his first touchdown as a pro on a 10-yard run on the Raiders' opening offensive possession. He'll seek to build on the initial start of his career next Sunday at Denver.

short_comment: Washington compiled eight rushes for 23 yards and secured his only target for four yards during Sunday's 21-13 defeat to the Seahawks.
long_comment: Aside from a 25-carry outburst in Week 8 at the Jets, Washington has logged 54 rushes along with four catches in nine appearances, which amounts to 6.4 touches per game. Despite that number, he continues to eat into the overall backfield picture, as lead runner Ashton Jeanty failed to tally double-digit rushes for a fourth straight contest Sunday. Washington should retain a modest role alongside Jeanty next Sunday at Denver.

short_comment: Jeanty turned his nine carries into just 18 yards and caught all four of his targets for 46 yards during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
long_comment: After reaching the 10-carry threshold in each of the first six games of the season, Jeanty has failed to do so in four straight contests, and he also has fallen shy of 30 rushing yards in six consecutive outings. Rookie RB Mike Washington continued to split the backfield with Jeanty in Week 10, turning his nine touches into 27 yards from scrimmage. Considering recent trends, Jeanty is difficult to trust for consistent production without a boost in work.

short_comment: Paye (neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
long_comment: Paye exited the second half of Sunday's game with a neck injury. The linebacker logged five tackles before departing. Malcolm Koonce will likely finish the game at strongside linebacker opposite Maxx Crosby.

short_comment: Benson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
long_comment: Benson is a healthy scratch for a third consecutive week. The rookie sixth-rounder has failed to find a place in a wide-open receiving corps so far, and it remains to be seen how coach Klint Kubiak will utilize him.

short_comment: Booker (ankle) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
long_comment: Booker was a full participant in Friday's practice but remained questionable headed into the weekend. The defensive lineman appears to not be quite ready to suit up, leaving JJ Pegues to see more defensive snaps in Sunday's contest.

short_comment: Thornton (back) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
long_comment: Thornton was a late addition to the Raiders' injury report due to a back issue. It's been determined by medical staff that the second-year wide receiver will not play in Sunday's contest, and Thornton has yet to play in a regular-season game in 2026 after appearing in 15 contests during his rookie campaign. Dareke Young and Cody White will operate as the depth options at wide receiver behind Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech.

short_comment: The Raiders elevated Runyon from their practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
long_comment: Runyon began the season on IR due to a foot injury. He was activated Nov. 4 but was then waived the following day. Runyon subsequently returned to Las Vegas as part of the practice squad and could get his first regular-season game action of the campaign Sunday. However, the Raiders have three tight ends ahead of him on the depth chart (Brock Bowers, Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas), so Runyon may be limited to special teams if he does suit up.

short_comment: Zuhn (concussion) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Zuhn started Week 10 prep with a pair of limited practices before upgrading to full participation in Friday's session. The starting left guard has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and is all set to suit up for Sunday's game against the defending champion Seahawks.

short_comment: Fatukasi (shoulder/back) was a full participant at practice Thursday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
long_comment: Fatukasi popped up on the Raiders' injury report Wednesday with shoulder and back issues, but it seems like those were minor, and he's in line to suit up in Week 10. He figures to start on the defensive line Sunday versus the Seahawks.

short_comment: Stukes registered five tackles (three solo) and an interception during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.
long_comment: Stukes jumped in front of a Brock Purdy pass intended for George Kittle midway through the third quarter, although the Raiders' offense gave the ball right back to the 49ers two plays later on a Brock Bowers fumble. It was the second interception of the season for Stukes, who was a second-round selection of the Raiders in the 2026 NFL Draft. The rookie out of Arizona is up to 43 tackles (23 solo) and four pass defenses through the first eight regular-season games of his NFL career.

short_comment: Chinn recorded nine tackles (six solo) during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.
long_comment: Chinn finished Week 9 as the Raiders' third-leading tackler behind Nakobe Dean (19) and Quay Walker (11). Dean has logged at least seven stops in five consecutive outings, and he has accumulated 66 tackles (44 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception), two forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries over nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Walker posted 11 tackles (three solo) during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.
long_comment: It was the second time in three games that Walker finished with double-digit stops, and he finished second on the Raiders in tackles behind Nakobe Dean (19). Walker is on track for his fifth consecutive 100-plus tackle campaign and is up to 72 stops (28 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Dean logged 19 tackles (seven solo) during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.
long_comment: Dean played every defensive snap and was all over the field in Week 9, finishing with a career-best 19 total tackles. He's logged at least 12 tackles in six of his last seven outings, and through nine regular-season games he has accumulated 98 total tackles, which is second-most in the NFL behind Alex Singleton (107).

short_comment: O'Connell moves to QB No. 2 on the depth chart behind Fernando Mendoza, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: O'Connell is set to back up rookie Mendoza, who replaced recently traded Kirk Cousins as the starting quarterback. O'Connell has been with Las Vegas since the team drafted him in the fourth round of the 2023 NFL Draft. The 28-year-old last appeared in a regular-season game in 2025, completing 10 of 22 attempts for 102 yards.

short_comment: Bech caught one of two targets for nine yards Sunday in a loss to the 49ers.
long_comment: Bech logged a 34 percent offensive snap share, third-highest among Raiders wideouts behind Jalen Nailor (74 percent) and Tre Tucker (64 percent). Though he seems fairly secure in the No. 3 wideout role, Bech hasn't done much this season, producing no more than three catches or 25 yards in any of his five games to date.

short_comment: Awosika (fibula) is active for Monday's game against the Ravens.
long_comment: Awosika will suit up Monday for the first time since Week 2, when he suffered an injury to his fibula. He should slide back into his starting role at left guard.

short_comment: Eboigbe (ankle) is inactive for Monday's game against the Ravens, Omar Navarro of the Chargers' official site reports.
long_comment: Eboigbe suffered an ankle injury against the Texans in Week 9, and he will be sidelined for Monday night's contest. Nick Barrett should see an uptick in defensive snaps in the absence of Eboigbe, whose next chance to play is Week 11 against the Jets on Nov. 22.

short_comment: Njoku (fibula) is officially listed as active Monday night's game against the Ravens, Omar Navarro of the Chargers' official site reports.
long_comment: Since being designated for return from IR on Nov. 4, Njoku -- who last played in Week 2 -- logged five consecutive limited practice listings before upgrading to full participation Saturday and being deemed questionable for Monday's contest. With his return to the lineup now confirmed, Njoku will bolster a TE corps that also includes Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden. In his only full game with the team this season, Njoku caught all five of his targets for 58 yards in a Week 1 loss to the Cardinals. Now that he's back in the mix, the 2017 first-rounder has an opportunity to reclaim enough of a role in the 0-8 Chargers offense to merit fantasy lineup consideration at his position in deeper fantasy formats going forward.

short_comment: Pipkins (knee), who is currently on injured reserve, will not play in Monday's game against the Ravens.
long_comment: Pipkins hasn't played since Week 1. Although he recently had his 21-day practice window opened, he won't suit up Monday night. Pipkins' next opportunity to get on the field will come in Week 11 against the Jets.

short_comment: Taylor (ankle) was placed on injured reserve Monday.
long_comment: Taylor is battling an ankle injury and was ruled out for the Week 10 meeting with Baltimore. Now on injured reserve, he will be required to miss at least four games before being eligible to return.

short_comment: The Chargers activated Perryman (pectoral) from the reserve/injured list ahead of Monday's game versus Baltimore.
long_comment: Perryman is finally cleared to suit up after missing the entire season due to a pec issue. While his return is good news for the Chargers, it may take him a game or two to get back to full speed.

short_comment: The Chargers list Thompson (hamstring) as doubtful for Monday's game against the Ravens.
long_comment: Though Thompson appears to have moved past the quadriceps injury he sustained Week 2, the Chargers have been listing him with a hamstring issue since returning from their Week 7 bye. The rookie wideout didn't practice in any capacity this week, but he apparently displayed enough progress to avoid being ruled out in advance of Monday's contest. Even so, Thompson isn't expected to play and will likely be included on the Chargers' inactive list, which will be released 90 minutes prior to the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff.

short_comment: Leonard (concussion) does not have a designation for Monday's matchup against Baltimore.
long_comment: Leonard suffered a concussion at some point between the Chargers' Week 6 loss to Kansas City and the team's Week 7 bye. He missed the club's past two contests but has now passed through the NFL's concussion protocol and has been cleared to return to game action. Leonard should assume a rotational role in Los Angeles' secondary.

short_comment: Mitchell (hip) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Ravens.
long_comment: Mitchell's practice reps were limited by a hip injury, but he's been officially cleared to play Monday against the team he spent three seasons with from 2023 to 2025. He turned 10 touches into 67 yards during the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, and Mitchell will continue to operate in a rotational role in the backfield alongside Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal.

short_comment: Hart (ankle) practiced in full Friday.
long_comment: Hart upgraded to full participation in Friday's practice after being limited during Thursday's session. The cornerback therefore should be set to suit up for Monday night's contest against the Ravens.

short_comment: Harris (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice.
long_comment: After being limited the day before, Harris erased any doubt about his availability for Monday's game at Baltimore. He saw a team-high seven targets on a 79 percent route share last week, catching three passes for a mere six yards in the 44-22 loss to Houston. Harris' volume projection for Week 10 partially depends on Ladd McConkey (back), who didn't play any snaps last week and didn't practice Thursday or Friday.

short_comment: Herbert (finger) doesn't appear on the the Chargers' injury report ahead of Monday night's game against the Ravens.
long_comment: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh previously noted that the QB "should be good to go" for Week 10 action after imaging on Herbert's injured left middle finger came back negative for a fracture, per ESPN.com. The fact that Herbert isn't listed in any way on the team's first injury report this week aligns with that and paves the way for him to continue to helm the offense for 0-8 Los Angeles versus Baltimore.

short_comment: Henley remains with the Chargers, as the Broncos have backed out of trading for the linebacker, Jeff Legwold of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: A trade involving Henley was agreed to Tuesday pending a physical, but the Broncos apparently found a red flag concerning his knee during that physical. Denver offered an updated trade to the Chargers with different draft compensation than the originally agreed upon 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick, but the two sides were unable to agree on an updated framework, so Henley will ultimately remain with the Chargers. Henley has not missed a game this season, so the concern Denver discovered on his physical isn't expected to impact his availability for Monday's game against the Ravens.

short_comment: Lambert-Smith registered one catch (on four targets) for 50 yards in Sunday's loss to Houston.
long_comment: Lambert-Smith wasn't exactly prolific in spite of logging a hearty 40 offensive snaps, but he made his one catch count, hauling in a 50-yard reception in the third quarter. However, the woeful Chargers turned the ball over on a fumble two plays later. Lambert-Smith has spent much of the season on IR and has had an inconsistent role when suiting up, but he was deployed pretty heavily Sunday because Ladd McConkey couldn't play due to back spasms. If McConkey is also sidelined next Monday in Baltimore, Lambert-Smith could again be a fairly big part of Los Angeles' air attack.

short_comment: Vidal rushed seven times for 30 yards in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. He added one catch for six yards on three targets.
long_comment: The Chargers continue to use a three-man backfield, an unfriendly fantasy situation and one to avoid when making lineup decisions each week. Vidal has been productive when he does get touches, rushing 36 times for 162 yards (4.5 YPC) and one touchdown across eight games. He's also caught 10 passes for 56 yards and an additional score.

short_comment: Gadsden caught two of three targets for 17 yards during the Chargers' 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday.
long_comment: Gadsden was on the field for 33 of 72 offensive snaps (45.8 percent), which was second-most among Chargers tight ends behind Charlie Kolar (47). Gadsden has caught two passes or fewer in six of eight regular-season games, and his 19-172-1 receiving line (on 29 targets) is well behind pace from his rookie campaign (49 catches on 69 targets for 664 yards and three scores across 15 regular-season contests). The Chargers' offense this season has struggled under quarterback Justin Herbert and coordinator Mike McDaniel, which doesn't bring much confidence ahead of their Week 10 road tilt against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

short_comment: Kolar brought in all three of his targets for 31 yards in a 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday.
long_comment: Kolar has recorded three catches in four of his last five outings, although he's cracked 30-plus receiving yards in just two of those contests. The Chargers average a season-low 15.1 points per game, and their 201.9 receiving yards per game is ninth-fewest in the NFL, making pass catchers like Kolar hard to rely on for sustained production. The 0-8 Chargers will look to capture their first win of the season in Week 10 against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

short_comment: Dicker went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 44-22 loss to Houston.
long_comment: Dicker was able to make multiple field-goal tries for the third straight game and fifth time this season. The kicker did all his damage in the first half, converting field goals from 52, 33 and 43 yards before the break. Dicker has now gone 15-for-17 on field-goal attempts, including 1-for-2 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far during the 2026 campaign.
