short_comment: Smith caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
long_comment: With the Rams down both Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) for the first time this season, Smith operated as the fourth receiver against Arizona, playing nine of 76 offensive snaps. His 22-yard touchdown in the second quarter was the first of Smith's career. Based on his small amount of playing time and routes run, Smith's 12-point PPR day isn't worth chasing in fantasy.

short_comment: Mumpfield brought in three of four targets for 81 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) on injured reserve, Mumpfield operated as the de facto No. 1 receiver for Matthew Stafford. Mumpfield met the moment with a team-high receiving yardage total that more than doubled that of the next-closest pass catcher, Xavier Smith (40 yards). The 2025 seventh-round pick has now cleared the 80-yard mark twice this season, but Mumpfield could slide down to the No. 2 role in a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve home matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25 if Adams is able to finish his recovery over the upcoming Week 11 bye.

short_comment: Stafford completed 18 of 26 passes for 249 yards with three touchdowns and one interception and rushed twice for minus-2 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: Stafford didn't let the fact he was without top wideouts Puka Nacua (IR, knee/toe) and Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) deter him from a very fantasy-friendly performance, as the reigning NFL MVP tossed at least three TD passes for the fourth time this season. Stafford connected with the unlikely trio of Tyler Higbee (five yards), Xavier Smith (22 yards) and Davis Allen (19 yards) for his scoring strikes, and the quarterback's 9.6 yards per attempt was his second-highest figure of the season. Stafford, who'll have a chance to further build chemistry with his current wideouts during the Week 11 bye, could have Adams back for a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25, as reports earlier Sunday indicated the talented wideout is targeting that game for his return.

short_comment: Williams rushed 12 times for 23 yards and brought in two of five targets for nine yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: Williams was held well under 4.0 yards per carry for the third consecutive game, but Sunday's performance was particularly alarming in that he averaged a minuscule 1.9 yards per carry. In contrast, Blake Corum (17-100-1) and Ronnie Rivers (15-81-0, albeit in garbage time) both had multiple productive runs on the way to efficient afternoons, making Williams' struggles stand out all the more. With Corum particularly playing well in the last several weeks, Williams could be relegated to a clear complementary role in a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve home showdown with the Packers on Nov. 25, following a Week 11 bye.

short_comment: Corum rushed 17 times for 100 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of four targets for 19 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: Corum was far more productive than backfield mate Kyren Williams, who he outpaced by five carries and 77 rushing yards. It was the fourth straight game with double-digit rush attempts and a touchdown for Corum, with Sunday's score coming from one yard out early in the third quarter. He has at least 73 rushing yards in three of the last four contests, and it remains to be seen if Sunday's division of labor will have any sticking power when Los Angeles returns to action following a Week 11 bye in a Week 12 home Thanksgiving Eve matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25.

short_comment: Shelton (hamstring) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
long_comment: With both Shelton and backup center Dylan McMahon (knee) ruled out, the Rams' offensive line depth has become razor-thin. David Quessenberry or Beaux Limmer will likely finish the game at center for the team.

short_comment: Cardona (ankle) is inactive for Sunday's game against Arizona.
long_comment: Cardona will end up missing a third consecutive game while recovering from an ankle injury, and his next chance to play is Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Jake McQuaide will once again serve as the Rams' long snapper.

short_comment: McDuffie (back) is active for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
long_comment: McDuffie missed three of the Rams' last four games due to a persistent back injury. The cornerback is all set to suit up for Sunday's game, as he and Kam Curl return to reinforce the Rams' secondary in time for a divisional matchup with the Cardinals' rookie quarterback Carson Beck.

short_comment: Curl (toe) is active for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
long_comment: Curl's sole limited practice session Friday was enough to cement his availability for Sunday's contest. The strong safety has started every contest for the Rams in 2026, playing 100 percent of the defensive snaps in six of the Rams' nine games.

short_comment: Allen (oblique) is active for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
long_comment: Allen has recovered enough from the oblique injury he suffered during the Rams' Week 9 win over the Commanders to suit up for Week 10. The No. 3 tight end is a key part of the Rams' 13-personnel offense, and he should continue seeing a significant share of offensive snaps for the team.

short_comment: Simpson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Rams' emergency third quarterback in Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
long_comment: Simpson continues to be inactive behind Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett. The quarterback will only enter the game if both Stafford and Bennett must exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

short_comment: Garrett (knee) is listed as active Sunday at Arizona, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
long_comment: Garrett was listed as limited on the Rams' first two Week 10 practice reports due to a knee injury and then got a veteran's rest day Friday, heading into the weekend listed as questionable. Head coach Sean McVay told Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com on Friday that Garrett is expected to play Sunday, which now has been confirmed. Garrett will be looking to have a similar impact to the 3.0-sack day he had in Week 9 against the Commanders.

short_comment: According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN,  Adams (hamstring) is believed to be targeting a return to action Nov. 25 against the Packers.
long_comment: Rapoport also noted Sunday that Adams' fellow WR Puka Nacua (knee/toe) has an estimated return in the mid-December range. For now, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell are in line to lead the WR corps of the Rams (who are on bye in Week 11), with CJ Daniels, Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley also on hand.

short_comment: Nacua (knee/toe) has an expected return date of "mid-December," Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
long_comment: After the Rams placed Nacua on injured reserve Thursday, Nacua must miss at least four games, which means his earliest return date is Sunday, Dec. 20 against the Cowboys. Considering the timeline given in Rapoport's report, Nacua thus may miss only the minimum number of contests while on IR after suffering PCL and MCL sprains and also a turf-toe injury last Sunday at Washington. With Davante Adams (hamstring) out at least one more outing, L.A. is rolling with a receiving corps of Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels, Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley in Week 10.

short_comment: Head coach Sean McVay said Friday that Daniels "will get an opportunity to play more snaps moving forward," Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
long_comment: Daniels has seen minimal playing time this season, but he'll be thrust into a more prominent role offensively due to both Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) being on injured reserve. As such, Daniels -- a sixth-round selection of the Rams in the 2026 NFL Draft -- is slated to serve as the team's WR3 behind Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, with Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley also in the mix for snaps on offense. During his final college season in Miami, Daniels recorded 50 catches for 557 yards and seven touchdowns across 13 games.

short_comment: Parkinson (ribs) and Tyler Higbee (illness) have been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Cardinals, while fellow tight end Davis Allen (oblique) is listed as questionable, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Parkinson hasn't shown much hint of matching last year's TD-fueled fantasy production, but he could see more targets in the coming weeks with both Puka Nacua (knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) on injured reserve. Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell are the favorites for WR snaps, likely leaving the RBs and TEs to handle a larger-than-usual portion of Matthew Stafford's targets. Of course, the Rams will probably want to run the ball more often while their top receiving weapons are sidelined.

short_comment: Higbee (illness) and Colby Parkinson (rib) have both been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Cardinals, while fellow tight end Davis Allen (oblique) is listed as questionable, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: With wideout Puka Nacua (knee) placed on injured reserve this week, there's renewed fantasy interest in the Rams' tight ends. Higbee has run a lot of routes without providing production in recent games, but both he and Parkinson could see more targets over the next few weeks, including Sunday in a favorable matchup with Arizona's subpar pass defense.

short_comment: The Rams signed Presley to the 53-man roster Thursday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
long_comment: Los Angeles is hurting at wide receiver, so the team signed Presley to bolster depth. The 24-year-old has appeared in just one game during his NFL career since going undrafted in 2025, though he spent all of his time on special teams.

short_comment: Landman recorded seven tackles (three solo), one pass breakup and a forced fumble in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.
long_comment: Much like last season, when Landman set a career high with 132 tackles across 17 starts, he's racking up the tackles through eight games in 2026. The middle linebacker is up to 66 tackles (37 solo), three forced fumbles and two pass breakups on 86 percent of the defensive snaps. Interestingly, Landman's snaps have been cut some since he returned from a concussion in Week 8. Over the last two weeks, he's played less than 70 percent of the defensive snaps after playing more than 90 percent across Weeks 1 through 6.

short_comment: Phillips underwent further tests Monday on his arm injured in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports.
long_comment: Phillips was seen wearing an arm sling after Sunday's Week 10 loss to the Colts. Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said they have "concerns" about the injury but had no more updates to add. Keith Cooper and Kenneth Grant will likely see more snaps should Phillips miss time.

short_comment: Coach Jeff Hafley said Monday that it has yet to be determined whether Willis (abdomen) will need surgery to address his groin/core injury.David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
long_comment: Per Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald, on that subject Hafley noted Monady, "we will see how he feels. If he needs surgery, he will have surgery," while adding that if the QB does undergo a procedure, it wouldn't "necessarily" be season-ending. In any case, the earliest Willis can come off IR is Week 14, with Kyle McCord and Brady Cook currently available to handle Miami's signal-caller duties.

short_comment: Traore went without a target while playing six of the Dolphins' 69 snaps on offense in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
long_comment: Meanwhile, Traore tied a season-high with 23 snaps on special teams, where he continues to receive the bulk of his playing time. The reserve tight end has played in all nine of the Dolphins' games to date but has gone without a reception while being targeted once across 39 total snaps on offense.

short_comment: Dulcich failed to haul in either of his two targets while logging 42 of 69 offensive snaps in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
long_comment: Second-year signal-caller Kyle McCord threw for 209 yards on 32 attempts in his first NFL start, but he couldn't forge much of a connection with Dulcich, who was held without a catch for the second time this season. With Malik Willis (core) out for at least three more contests while on injured reserve, Dulcich will have more time to build a rapport with McCord, but the tight end was far from a reliable fantasy option even when Willis was directing the offense. Despite playing more than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in each of the Dolphins' nine games, Dulcich has been limited to 24 receptions for 270 yards and has yet to find the end zone.

short_comment: Tolbert caught both of his targets for 49 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
long_comment: The wideout was active for just the fifth time in nine games this season and played 11 of 69 offensive snaps. He ran only five routes and caught a 34-yard touchdown from fellow receiver Malik Washington on a trick play early in the second quarter. Tolbert has no fantasy appeal moving forward, as he has just four catches for 79 yards on six targets this season.

short_comment: Washington secured all three targets for 50 yards, threw a 34-yard touchdown on his one pass attempt and returned four punts for 36 yards in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
long_comment: Washington finished second in receiving yards for the Dolphins and also was partly responsible for the team's one score through the air, uncorking a well-thrown 34-yard strike to Jalen Tolbert on a trick play. Washington also continued to produce in his returner role, and he's now up to 812 all-purpose yards through nine games heading into a Week 11 road matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

short_comment: Douglas brought in three of eight targets for 71 yards in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
long_comment: Douglas posted a team-high yardage total with a big hand from his game-long 38-yard grab. Douglas garnered plenty of first-time starter Kyle McCord's attention as evidenced by the receiver's team-high target tally, and he's now hit or exceeded the 70-yard mark in three of the past four games. The 2026 third-round pick will look to carry over the momentum into a tough Week 11 road matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

short_comment: McCord completed 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed twice for four yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble that was returned for a touchdown.
long_comment: Drawing his first career start as a result of Malik Willis having gone on injured reserve with an abdomen injury earlier in the week, McCord acquitted himself well overall in a favorable matchup. The 2025 sixth-round pick of the Eagles spread the ball around to nine different targets, and he had a statement three-yard touchdown run on the first play of the fourth quarter when he powered through a pair of defenders and broke the plane despite having his facemask pulled. McCord's one turnover was very costly, however, as it was recovered on the Dolphins' six-yard line and returned for a short touchdown. McCord should only get more comfortable by following up Sunday's solid showing with another week of practice, but he'll draw a tough Week 11 road matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

short_comment: Gordon rushed 20 times for 76 and brought in four of five targets for 39 yards in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
long_comment: Filling his customary workhorse role in Miami's ground attack, Gordon handled all but four of the Dolphins' running back carries while finishing with a team-high reception total. The second-year back eclipsed 75 rushing yards for the fourth time in six games in the process, and Gordon's catch and receiving yardage totals were also season highs. Gordon should remain in a high-volume role in a Week 11 road matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

short_comment: Meyer (stinger) is questionable to return to Sunday's matchup against Indianapolis.
long_comment: Meyer started Sunday in place of Aaron Brewer, who was unable to suit up due to a concussion. With Meyer now at least temporarily sidelined, Jarrett Kingston has taken over at center for Miami.

short_comment: Biggers (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Colts, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports.
long_comment: Biggers injured his knee late in the first quarter, and medical staff has determined that the second-year defensive tackle's injury is severe enough for him to be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's contest. Keith Cooper and Kenneth Grant will both see more rotational snaps on the defensive line in Biggers' absence.

short_comment: Baker (knee) was not activated from the reserve/PUP list ahead of Sunday's clash against Indianapolis.
long_comment: Baker was designated to return to practice Wednesday, but he isn't yet ready for game action. The veteran cornerback hasn't yet played for Miami after signing a one-year contract to join the organization last March. Baker's next chance to suit up will be Sunday, Nov. 22, in Buffalo.

short_comment: The Dolphins elevated Reagor from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
long_comment: The move gives the Dolphins extra depth at wide receiver, as rookie third-rounder Chris Bell (knee) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Colts. If Reagor sees the field in Week 10, then it would be the veteran wide receiver's first regular-season game since 2024, when he logged seven catches (on 12 targets) for 100 yards across eight games as a member of the Chargers.

short_comment: The Dolphins elevated Cook from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
long_comment: The Dolphins placed Malik Willis (abdomen) on injured reserve Tuesday, so Cook will operate as the team's backup quarterback behind Kyle McCord for Sunday's game against the Colts. Cook appeared in five regular-season games (four starts) for the Jets in 2025, when he completed 57.5 percent of his passes for 739 yards, two touchdowns and seven interceptions while rushing for 49 yards on 13 carries.

short_comment: Kacmarek (quadriceps) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
long_comment: Kacmarek upgraded his practice participation in each Week 10 prep session. The tight end went from a non-participant Wednesday to a full participant by Friday's session. Kacmarek is all set to suit up as the No. 2 tight end behind Greg Dulcich for Sunday's game against the Colts.

short_comment: Brooks recorded 12 tackles (four solo) during Sunday's 19-9 loss versus the Lions.
long_comment: Brooks played all 59 of the Dolphins' defensive snaps in Week 9, and he compiled a double-digit tackle total for the fourth time in his last six games. He's easily on pace for his sixth consecutive 100-tackle season going into a Week 10 matchup at Indianapolis.

short_comment: Rodriguez recorded 10 tackles (seven solo) including 1.0 sacks during Sunday's 19-9 loss versus the Lions.
long_comment: Rodriguez and the entire Dolphins defense performed well against a strong Detroit offense in Week 9, especially against the run. Rodriguez also recorded the first sack of his pro career late in the first quarter, pushing quarterback Jared Goff out of bounds for no gain. He ranks seventh in the NFL in total tackles on the season going into a Week 10 tilt at Indianapolis.

short_comment: Van Ginkel (quadriceps) is expected to practice in preparation for Week 11, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reported Monday.
long_comment: Van Ginkel sustained a quad injury late in Sunday's game against Green Bay. The 31-year-old has yet to miss a regular-season game in 2026, recording 28 tackles (16 solo), including 8.5 sacks, one pass deflection and one interception in nine contests.

short_comment: Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday that Addison will require surgery on his thumb and will miss a few weeks, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: O'Connell indicated that Addison will be a candidate for injured reserve, though if he does end up being deactivated, the Vikings anticipate that the wideout would be able to return after sitting out the minimum four games. Addison injured his thumb at Friday's practice and subsequently was inactive for Sunday's 30-10 win over Green Bay. For as long as Addison is sidelined, Jauan Jennings (calf), Myles Price and Tai Felton will be the options to see added reps behind No. 1 receiver Justin Jefferson.

short_comment: Coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday that the Vikings expect Hockenson (wrist/chest) to make progress ahead of Sunday's game against the 49ers, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Hockenson was inactive for Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers, but it sounds like the tight end has a chance to return to practice after logging 'DNPs' last week. In his absence versus Green Bay in Week 10, fellow TE Gavin Bartholomew caught three of his four targets for 36 yards and a TD.

short_comment: Bartholomew caught three of four targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
long_comment: With T.J. Hockenson (wrist) inactive, Bartholomew played 53 of 69 offensive snaps against Green Bay and caught the second of Kirk Cousins' two touchdowns, scoring from 20 yards out in the fourth quarter to give Minnesota a comfortable 27-10 lead. While Ben Yurosek got the start, Bartholomew played 13 more snaps and out-targeted Yurosek four to one. Cousins has an affinity for throwing to his tight ends, so Bartholomew will be on the fantasy radar if Hockenson needs to miss more time.

short_comment: Price caught all four targets for 49 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
long_comment: With Jordan Addison (thumb) inactive, Price moved up the depth chart and played 33 of 69 offensive snaps behind Justin Jefferson (63) and Tai Felton (59) in Kirk Cousins' 2026 debut with the team. Price ended up running 22 routes on Cousins' 36 dropbacks and produced the game's first touchdown, scoring from 38 yards out in the first quarter to give Minnesota a 10-0 lead. On limited offensive playing time this season, Price has recorded 10 catches for 81 yards and the one touchdown on 15 targets. He's unlikely to be a fantasy factor moving forward.

short_comment: Jones carried the ball 11 times for 47 yards and a touchdown and caught his only target for eight yards in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
long_comment: Jordan Mason led the Vikings with 59 rushing yards, but Jones had the more productive afternoon as he scored his first TD since Week 5 on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Jones' upside will remain limited while working in a timeshare with Mason, but he's still got some utility heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.

short_comment: Mason carried the ball 16 times for 59 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
long_comment: The fifth-year RB led the Vikings in rushing yards, but Aaron Jones was the more productive player in the backfield, gaining 55 scrimmage yards on 12 touches and scoring on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Mason has yet to get into the end zone in four games since returning from a thumb injury, piecing together 182 rushing yards on 4.0 yards per carry while working in a timeshare with Jones. He could break that drought in Week 11 in a potential revenge game against the 49ers.

short_comment: Cousins completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. He added 11 rushing yards on three carries.
long_comment: Brought back to Minnesota at the trade deadline to stabilize the offense, Cousins did exactly that, connecting with Myles Price for a 38-yard TD in the first quarter and Gavin Bartholomew on a 20-yard score in the fourth while guiding Justin Jefferson to season highs in catches and targets. The Vikings' passing game didn't need to over-extend itself, however, as the defense sacked Jordan Love eight times in another dominant performance. Cousins may need to find another gear in Week 11 against the 49ers, but he'll have another week of practice to re-familiarize himself with Kevin O'Connell's scheme first.

short_comment: Jefferson caught nine of 13 targets for 74 yards in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
long_comment: In Kirk Cousins' return to the Vikings, Jefferson led the team in catches, targets and receiving yards, although Myles Price and Gavin Bartholomew were on the other end of the QB's two touchdown passes. The nine grabs and 13 targets were season highs for Jefferson, while the yardage total was his best showing since Week 5. Despite a disappointing 40-467-4 line on 64 targets through eight games, the star wideout's outlook for the rest of the year is pointed up heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.

short_comment: Jones (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Packers.
long_comment: Jones is being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's game. He was a practice squad elevation Saturday to give the Vikings more depth at wide receiver due to the absences of both Jordan Addison (thumb) and Jauan Jennings (calf).

short_comment: Richter (foot) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Packers.
long_comment: Richter injured his foot in the first quarter, and medical staff have determined that the injury is severe enough for the third-year linebacker to be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's contest. Richter's playing time this season has primarily come on special teams, and his availability for Week 11 against the 49ers on Nov. 22, is up in the air.

short_comment: Van Noy (calf) is active for Sunday's game against the Packers.
long_comment: Van Noy tweaked his calf during the Vikings' Week 9 loss to the Bills. He earned the questionable tag for Week 10 after logging a limited practice Friday, and he was cleared by medical staff to play in Sunday's NFC North showdown. Van Noy has 15 tackles (nine solo), including 1.5 sacks, through eight regular-season games.

short_comment: Metellus (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Packers.
long_comment: Metellus was added to the Vikings' practice report Friday due to a shoulder issue, but the injury won't prevent the seventh-year pro from suiting up for Sunday's NFC North showdown. He has 58 tackles (29 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and four pass defenses through eight regular-season games.

short_comment: Culp was elevated from the Vikings' practice squad to their active roster Saturday.
long_comment: Culp signed with Minnesota's practice squad Oct. 28, and this is his first elevation since joining the organization. He last suited up for regular-season action in 2025 for Tampa Bay, when he caught his only target over 13 games for a six-yard touchdown. Assuming Culp is active Sunday, he'll boost the depth of a Vikings tight-end corps that will be without starter T.J. Hockenson (wrist).

short_comment: Wentz (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Green Bay, but Kirk Cousins will be Minnesota's starting quarterback.
long_comment: Kyler Murray (hamstring) is out for another week but may eventually replace Wentz as the No. 2 quarterback. Wentz's miserable performance against the Bills last week likely was a factor in the Vikings trading for Cousins.

short_comment: Wilson recorded nine tackles (three solo) in Monday night's 23-6 loss to the Bills.
long_comment: The veteran linebacker has started all eight games this season, logging 94 percent of the defensive snaps for Minnesota. He's now up to 50 tackles (24 solo), including 3.0 sacks, seven QB hits and a pass breakup. He's been extremely productive under defensive coordinator Brian Flores over the last two seasons, recording 9.5 sacks as an off-bal linebacker across 25 regular-season games during that span.

short_comment: Felton went without a target while playing six of the Vikings' 48 offensive snaps in Monday's 23-6 loss to the Bills.
long_comment: Felton continues to handle a muted role as a depth receiver for Minnesota, as Monday marked the third consecutive game in which he played single-digit snaps. For the season, the second-year wideout out of Maryland has been limited to just three receptions for 41 yards on seven targets over eight appearances.

short_comment: Dallas caught his only target for a two-yard gain in Monday's Week 9 loss to the Bills.
long_comment: Dallas notched just eight offensive snaps but also contributed 19 snaps on special teams. The veteran running back went without a carry for the fourth time over Minnesota's past five games, indicating his lack of a role in the running game. Overall this season, Dallas has been a very small part of the Vikings' offense, recording four carries for 14 yards and five catches for 36 yards (on five targets) through eight contests.

short_comment: Reichard made both of his field-goal attempts during the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday.
long_comment: After missing his lone field-goal attempt in Week 8 against the Lions, Reichard bounced back Monday to connect on field goals from 43 and 53 yards in the second quarter, which ended up being the only points that the Vikings scored. Reichard's 20 made field goals through eight regular-season games is tied for fourth-most in the NFL, and his seven makes from 50-plus yards is tied with Ka'imi Fairbairn for second behind Spencer Shrader (eight). The Vikings are 6-2 despite their struggles on offense this season, but the acquisition of Kirk Cousins should help make the unit more efficient. Minnesota will travel to Lambeau Field for Week 10 against Green Bay on Nov. 15.

short_comment: Mike Reiss of ESPN notes via ESPN's Adam Schefter that there are fears  DeVito's teammate, Drake Maye, may have sustained a fractured ankle during Week 10 action.
long_comment: Regarding Maye's status going forward, coach Mike Vrabel indicated that he'd wait for further information before estimating how long his starting QB might be out, but acknowledged he "wouldn't imagine him being available coming out of the (Week 11) bye," Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports. As a result, DeVito is in a position to start Nov. 29 against the Chargers, and possibly beyond. That said, as NFL reporter Jordan Schultz suggests, New England is expected to explore the QB market in the coming days, be it through a practice squad addition or a veteran free agent such as Jimmy Garoppolo, who has previously worked with  offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels.

short_comment: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that he didn't have a definitive diagnosis for the injury Maye (ankle) sustained in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich, but indicated that the quarterback will miss time," Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports.  "I wouldn't imagine him being available coming out of the [Week 11] bye," Vrabel said.
long_comment: Adam Schefter of ESPN reported earlier Monday that the Patriots were concerned that Maye fractured his ankle Sunday. That diagnosis has yet to be confirmed, however, and Vrabel suggested that he'll avoid projecting a timeline for Maye until the quarterback returns from Germany to be further evaluated. At the very least, Maye can be expected to miss the Patriots' next game Nov. 29 against the Chargers. In the meantime, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz suggests that the team is expected to explore the quarterback market in the coming days, though top backup Tommy DeVito is currently next in line to start in place of Maye.

short_comment: Brown (hamstring) was spotted walking around with a limp in the locker room following Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich, Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald reports.
long_comment: Brown returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries to suit up Sunday. However, the veteran wideout sustained a hamstring injury while making a reception in the third quarter and wasn't able to return to the contest. Brown didn't speak to reporters following the loss, and head coach Mike Vrabel said the team would "see what the severity of that [injury] is" once the team returns to the United States. New England is on bye Week 11, but it's far from certain Brown will be able to suit up the next time the team plays Nov. 29 against the Chargers.

short_comment: Borregales made his sole field-goal attempt and one PAT in the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich on Sunday.
long_comment: Borregales made a 33-yard field goal on the first drive of the game. The kicker is now 11-for-13 on field-goal attempts and 24-for-25 on PATs through 10 regular-season games in 2026.

short_comment: Douglas caught one of three passes for four yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
long_comment: The Patriots' offense was effective on the first drive of the game, but that was where the good news ended for New England after Drake Maye was knocked out for the rest of the contest due to an ankle injury. Tommy DeVito took over under center, and the offense struggled to move down the field for the rest of the game. For Douglas, it was the third time this season that he was held to one catch, with the last instance taking place in Week 3 against the Jaguars. A.J. Brown -- who was cleared to return from a two-game absence due to knee and ankle injuries -- also picked up a hamstring injury during Sunday's game, so Douglas could be the New England's WR1 following the Week 11 bye. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Henry caught two of three passes for 22 yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
long_comment: Both of Henry's catches of 10 and 12 yards came on the Patriots' first offensive drive of the game, which ended with a 33-yard field goal by Andy Borregales. Unfortunately for the Patriots, Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury on the play prior to the field goal and was unable to return, and the offense struggled to move down the field with backup Tommy DeVito under center. Maye will undergo more tests once the team has returned to home soil, but the good news for the Patriots is that they are on a bye for Week 11, so the third-year quarterback has more time to heal before New England's next game in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29. Henry's two catches Sunday were his fewest since Week 3 against the Jaguars (one), and the veteran tight end has a 34-383-2 receiving line on 40 targets through 10 regular-season games.

short_comment: Hollins caught five of six targets for 48 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich.
long_comment: In his second game back from a calf injury, Hollins led the Patriots in catches and receiving yards, but the entire offense was compromised when Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early. A.J. Brown (hamstring) also didn't last long in his latest return to action. New England gets a bye in Week 11, giving the team's injured stars a chance to recover, so Hollins' role and usage may not become clear until after the break. Over six appearances this season, Hollins has produced a 23-293-1 line on 32 targets.

short_comment: Kiner carried the ball 10 times for 25 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to Detroit.
long_comment: Rhamondre Stevenson was active despite dealing with a knee issue during the practice week, but the veteran back gained just four yards on six carries, and Kiner wound up leading the Patriots' backfield in both volume and yardage. The entire offense struggles after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, however. New England gets a Week 11 bye, so Kiner's role and usage for a Week 12 clash with the Chargers likely won't become clear until the health of Stevenson and Maye come into focus after the break.

short_comment: Stevenson carried the ball six times for four yards and caught his only target for one yard in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich.
long_comment: The whole Patriots' offense struggled after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, but Stevenson also didn't look to be in peak form after dealing with a knee issue during the practice week. Corey Kiner wound up leading the backfield with just 25 rushing yards on 10 totes. Stevenson will get a Week 11 bye to rest up, and if Maye's injury ends up sidelining him for an extended period, New England could lean heavily on its running game in Week 12 against the Chargers.

short_comment: Jones (cramps) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
long_comment: Jones left the game during the fourth quarter, and given the score of the contest, the veteran linebacker is unlikely to return to Sunday's game. If that's the case, then Jones will finish with two tackles (one solo) and one QB hit.

short_comment: Spillane (illness) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
long_comment: Spillane went to the locker room in the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's international game. Darius Muasau has taken over for Spillane at inside linebacker.

short_comment: Moses (knee) has returned to Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Moses went to the locker room in the first quarter to have his knee injury evaluated. He's been cleared by medical staff to return and is back in at right tackle, with backup Caleb Lomu now on the sidelines.

short_comment: Van Roten (hamstring) is active for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
long_comment: Van Roten will be available to make his season debut after spending the first nine weeks of the campaign on injured reserve due to the hamstring issue. He was able to practice throughout Week 10 prep, turning in a pair of a limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full activity Friday, and the Patriots activated him Saturday. With Ben Brown (knee) and Walter Rouse (concussion) inactive for the Germany game, Van Roten will likely draw the start at left guard.

short_comment: Woods (hamstring) is active for Sunday's game versus the Lions in Munich.
long_comment: Woods didn't suit up for a Week 9 loss to the Packers due to a hamstring injury, but he followed an LP/LP/FP practice regimen this week, which was enough to gain clearance to return to action. With Carlton Davis (knee) inactive Sunday, Woods is a good bet to enter the starting lineup at outside cornerback opposite Christian Gonzalez.

short_comment: Byard (chest) is active for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
long_comment: The veteran safety was listed as questionable heading into Sunday, but his ability to finish Week 10 prep with a full practice seemingly had him trending toward playing. He'll end up suiting up in Germany and isn't expected to face any limitations while he plays through the chest issue. Through New England's first nine games, Byard has compiled 43 tackles, three pass breakups and an interception.

short_comment: Gilliam (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
long_comment: Gilliam took a questionable tag into Sunday, but the Patriots' decision to activate him from injured reserve Saturday signaled that he was on track to play for the first time since Week 4. The fullback served almost exclusively as a blocker when he was healthy during the Patriots' first four games of the season, logging no carries and recording a four-yard reception on two targets.

short_comment: Henderson (illness) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Henderson was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, and now that he's on IR, the second-year running back will be required to miss at least the next four games. Henderson's next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Chiefs on Monday, Dec. 21, although there's no timetable for his return, as he is recovering from "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of neurological symptoms." If Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) cannot play Sunday, then the Patriots' backfield will be led by Corey Kiner and Lan Larison.

short_comment: Gonzalez logged 10 tackles (nine solo) and one pass defense during the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers in Week 9.
long_comment: Gonzalez's 10 stops were a season high, but the larger concern was his poor performance in coverage. Per Pro Football Focus, Gonzalez was on coverage for 11 catches for 192 yards and two touchdowns, and quarterback Jordan Love had a 158.3 passing rating while targeting the fourth-year defensive back. It wasn't the performance that the Patriots were expecting after signing Gonzalez to a lucrative four-year, $135 million contract extension in September. Things won't get easier for him or the Patriots' secondary, as they travel to Munich for Week 10 against the Lions, whose offense ranks fourth in the NFL in yards per game (379.8).

short_comment: Johnson caught two passes for 28 yards on three targets in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
long_comment: With Jordyn Tyson playing his second game since debuting last week, the rookie wideout was targeted 13 times on Tyler Shough's 35 pass attempts. It didn't leave much for the rest of New Orleans' pass catchers, as Travis Etienne was actually second on the team with five targets. Over his last five games, Johnson has nine catches for 85 yards and a score. He's become a low-end TE2 for fantasy.

short_comment: Estime carried the ball seven times for six yards and caught his only target for five yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to Carolina.
long_comment: Travis Etienne returned from IR and led the Saints' backfield with 11 touches, although he managed just 34 scrimmage yards, while Alvin Kamara handled five touches and scored two short TDs. Perhaps worse for Estime's role and future value, he was ineffective in short-yardage situations, getting stuffed on three attempts to pick up a first down from two yards out or less, and a miscommunication with Tyler Shough on a handoff led to a lost fumble in the second quarter, although the giveaway was charged to the QB. Estime will try to maintain some share of the workload in a Week 11 meeting with the Bears.

short_comment: Tyson caught 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
long_comment: That bang you just heard was the sound of the window closing on your chances of acquiring Tyson cheaply in your fantasy league. In just his second career NFL game, Tyson dominated looks from Tyler Shough, as no other New Orleans pass catcher handled more than five targets, hauled in more than three passes or topped 30 receiving yards. It may be tough for the team's struggling offense to keep both Tyson and Chris Olave busy at the same time, so the duo may end up trading big games rather than opening things up for each other, but this kind of volume can't be ignored. Tyson will look for his first career touchdown in a Week 11 tilt against the Bears.

short_comment: Etienne carried the ball eight times for 14 yards and caught three of five targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
long_comment: Seeing his first action since Week 3 after recovering from a hamstring strain, the former Jaguar led the Saints' backfield with 11 touches, ahead of Audric Estime's eight and Alvin Kamara's five. Etienne wasn't able to do much with the volume, however, while Kamara scored two short TDs. Etienne still appears to be the top option for the team at RB, but if Estime keeps taking short-yardage work and Kamara is the preferred red-zone back, it would put a real ceiling on Etienne's upside. He'll look to claim a bigger share of the workload in Week 11 against the Bears.

short_comment: Shough completed 25 of 35 targets for 187 yards and one touchdown with one interception in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. He added 25 rushing yards on six carries and was charged with a lost fumble.
long_comment: The second-year QB had more turnovers than TDs for only the second time this season, although his fumble may have been been more Audric Estime's fault, and Shough fell short of 200 passing yards for the third time. Rookie Jordyn Tyson was his top downfield option, catching 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards in a breakout performance, but no other Saint saw more than five targets or hauled in more than three passes. Shough will take a 15:7 TD:INT into a Week 11 clash with the Bears.

short_comment: Olave caught three of four targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
long_comment: The game wound up being Jordyn Tyson's breakout performance, as the rookie WR hauled in 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards, but that didn't leave much volume for Olave or any other Saint. With Tyler Shough struggling, it's unclear whether the passing game can keep more than one pass catcher fantasy-relevant at a time. Olave sports a 59-774-2 line on 87 targets through nine games, and he'll look to bounce back in a Week 11 tilt against the Bears.

short_comment: Kamra rushed two times for four yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. He added three catches for 10 yards and an additional touchdown on four targets.
long_comment: With Travis Etienne back from his weeks-long hamstring injury that saw him miss five games while on injured reserve, the Saints deployed a three-man backfield committee against Carolina. Kamara scored a couple touchdowns, but it was a fluky performance on just five touches and 16 offensive snaps. Audric Estime logged 27 snaps and handled eight touches, while Etienne played 21 snaps and touched the ball 11 times. This is a backfield to avoid in fantasy while it the trio cancels each other out and caps each others' upside.

short_comment: Richards (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against Carolina, Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio reports.
long_comment: Richards suffered a knee injury during the fourth quarter of Sunday's contest. Mason Murphy has taken over at right tackle in Richards' absence.

short_comment: Werner (hamstring) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Panthers, Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio reports.
long_comment: Werner left in the first half due to a hamstring injury, which medical staff has deemed severe enough for the sixth-year linebacker to be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's contest. Danny Stutsman will work alongside Kaden Elliss at inside linebacker in the absence of Werner, whose status for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22, is up in the air.

short_comment: Emerson (shin) is active for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
long_comment: Emerson drew the questionable tag for Sunday's NFC South tilt due to a nagging shin injury, but the fifth-year pro was given the green light by medical staff to play. He has 20 tackles (18 solo), four pass defenses (including two interceptions) and one forced fumble across seven regular-season games.

short_comment: The Saints placed Miller (knee) on injured reserve Saturday.
long_comment: Miller is dealing with a knee injury and is now required to miss at least four games. The rookie nose tackle has played in four games this season, logging five tackles (two solo) over 93 snaps on defense and four snaps on special teams. Nathan Shepherd and Khristian Boyd could both get more defensive snaps during Miller's absence.

short_comment: The Saints elevated Smyth from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday.
long_comment: Smyth is thus set to serve as the Saints' kicker for the second straight week. In his 2026 debut last Sunday against Cleveland, he went 3-for-4 on field-goal attempts and 2-for-2 on point-after tries. If Smyth performs well Sunday, he'll likely be elevated again for Week 11 in Chicago.

short_comment: Edwards (knee) does not have an injury designation against the Panthers on Sunday, Ross Jackson of WWL-TV reports.
long_comment: Edwards' practice reps were limited Wednesday and Thursday due to a knee injury, but he avoided an injury tag for Week 10 after logging a full session Friday. He has started in each of the Saints' first eight games of the regular season.

short_comment: Banks (ankle) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Ross Jackson of WWL-TV reports.
long_comment: Banks was able to avoid an injury tag after logging a full practice Friday. Sunday's game will be his second since being activated from injured reserve Nov. 7 due to a high-ankle sprain that he suffered in Week 2 against the Ravens.

short_comment: Fant Donaldson (back) upgraded to full participation at Thursday's practice.
long_comment: Fant was limited at Wednesday's practice, but the veteran TE faced no limitations Thursday, suggesting that he'll be good to go for Sunday's game against the Panthers. He has worked as the Saints' No. 2 option at the position behind Juwan Johnson.

short_comment: Granderson recorded seven tackles (five solo), including 2.0 sacks, and one pass defense during the Saints' 23-22 overtime win over the Browns in Week 9.
long_comment: Granderson took down Shedeur Sanders for sacks of six and nine yards in the second and third quarters, respectively. Granderson has logged at least 1.5 sacks in each of his last four outings, and his 7.5 sacks on the year are tied for fourth-most in the NFL and one shy from matching his career high in 2023. The Saints will stay home for Week 10 against the Panthers and Bryce Young, who has been sacked 26 times, which is fourth-most in the NFL.

short_comment: Elliss recorded 11 tackles (eight solo), including 1.0 sacks, during the Saints' 23-22 overtime victory over the Browns in Week 9.
long_comment: Elliss entered Week 9 without a sack to his name, but he changed that early in the first quarter after taking down Shedeur Sanders for a seven-yard loss. Elliss' 11 stops co-led the Saints, and the veteran linebacker is up to 41 tackles (23 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defense across five regular-season games.

short_comment: Brown caught his only target for 52 yards during Sunday's 23-22 overtime win versus the Browns. He also lost a fumble on a punt return.
long_comment: Brown showed off his plus speed in the second quarter, blowing by safety Ronnie Hickman and coming down with a 52-yard bomb from quarterback Tyler Shough. One series later, though, he coughed up the football during an erratic punt return. Barring an injury to one of the wideouts ahead of him on New Orleans' depth chart, there likely won't be much room in the short term for him to earn a significant role outside of special teams.

long_comment: out

short_comment: McFadden made 10 tackles (five solo) in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
long_comment: McFadden logged one tackle for loss in the contest. The starting inside linebacker assisted the Giants in holding the Commanders to 3.2 yards per carry and no rushing touchdowns in the game.

short_comment: Holland logged three tackles (one solo) and one pass defensed for an interception in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
long_comment: Holland picked off Jayden Daniels with 2:19 left in the fourth quarter, just one Commanders drive after Ar'Darius Washington picked the quarterback off. Despite back-to-back turnovers, the Giants' offense logged back-to-back three-and-outs to put the Commanders' offense in position to win the game.

short_comment: Washington accumulated seven tackles (five solo) and two passes defensed, including one interception, in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
long_comment: Washington broke up two passes in the contest, picking off Jayden Daniels with 5:31 left in the fourth quarter of Thursday's game. Despite making a crucial play with the Giants up four points, the offense could not put more points on the board to cement a primetime win.

short_comment: Reese logged 13 tackles (four solo) in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
long_comment: Reese led the Giants in tackles as a consistent force against the Commanders' run game in the NFC East showdown. Despite the rookie first-rounder's best efforts, the Giants allowed 24 points en route to a meaningful divisional loss.

short_comment: Zvada missed his only field-goal try and made all three of his PATs on Thursday in a loss to Washington.
long_comment: Zvada's miss was a chip-shot 33-yarder in the first quarter that sailed wide left. That proved to be a critical mistake, as the Commanders won by just three points. Zvada appeared to shore up his job security a bit by going 4-for-4 on FG tries in Week 9 against Philadelphia, but it's hard to ignore the fact that he's gone just 17-for-23 on field-goal attempts overall and has missed three kicks from under 50 yards. The rookie does have a perfect 16-for-16 mark on extra-point attempts, and head coach John Harbaugh expressed support for the inconsistent kicker Friday, saying of Zvada, "I'm confident that he's going to become a good kicker. If at some point and time it doesn't happen, it doesn't happen. But I'm not going to panic halfway through the season with a guy who has made a bunch of kicks," Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.

short_comment: Johnson logged one catch (on three targets) for eight yards Thursday in a loss to the Commanders.
long_comment: Johnson hasn't been able to get going in 2026, as he's finished with one or zero catches in six of his seven games so far. After working as New York's top tight end last season, he's been mostly an afterthought in the current campaign due to the arrival of Isaiah Likely, who went off for a 9-127-1 line on a team-leading 11 targets Thursday. As long as Likely is healthy, Johnson won't have much appeal in most fantasy formats.

short_comment: Mooney caught two of five targets for eight yards Thursday in a loss to Washington.
long_comment: Mooney logged the third-most targets of any New York pass catcher, but he managed just two short receptions. Efficiency has been an issue for the veteran wideout throughout the campaign, as he's hauled in only 14 of 30 targets through nine contests. Mooney has finished with fewer than 10 yards in four of his past six appearances, so he's not a viable fantasy play at the moment.

short_comment: Singletary played just five snaps on offense and took one carry for three yards in Thursday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders.
long_comment: Cam Skattebo came back from a hamstring injury and dominated backfield work, taking 21 touches for 122 yards and two touchdowns on an 88 percent snap share. Singletary played 92 percent of snaps the week before in a win at Philadelphia, but his 23 touches went for just 39 total yards and no TDs. It'll likely be another large workload for Skattebo when the Giants host the Jaguars in Week 11.

short_comment: Fields brought in three of four targets for 62 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
long_comment: The rookie finished a distant second in receiving yards to Isaiah Likely for the Giants on the night, but Fields' yardage total was the second highest of his nascent career. Fields has at least three catches in three consecutive games after opening his career with six straight two-reception efforts, and the Notre Dame product will look to continue cultivating his chemistry with J.J. McCarthy in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

short_comment: McCarthy completed 23 of 36 passes for 293 yards with a touchdown and an interception while adding six rushes for 34 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
long_comment: McCarthy continued to look like a competent NFL signal-caller in his third start for the Giants, posting a new career high in passing yards and adding a new season high in rushing yardage. His one touchdown pass was a critical one, as he hit Isaiah Likely over the middle for a 66-yard score just before the midway point of the fourth quarter to erase a 17-14 deficit. McCarthy has displayed excellent chemistry with his top targets, and he'll look to keep his hot streak going against a pass-funnel Jaguars defense in a Week 11 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 22.

short_comment: Nabers secured five of seven targets for 44 yards and lost a fumble in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
long_comment: The star wideout finished with less than 50 receiving yards for the second time in five days, and Nabers' late third-quarter lost fumble had significant ramifications. The turnover came at the Commanders' 16-yard line with the Giants down by three, costing  New York a golden opportunity to tie the game at minimum. Nabers' aforementioned pair of mediocre performances have come in the wake of a four-game streak of 100-yard efforts in Weeks 4-7, and he'll look to boost his numbers back up against the Jaguars' pass-funnel defense in a Week 11 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 22.

short_comment: Likely brought in nine of 11 targets for 127 yards and a touchdown and fumbled once but recovered in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
long_comment: Likely set the pace for the Giants across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his figure in the middle category also was a career high. The veteran tight end now has five double-digit target tallies on the campaign, and Thursday's production, which included a 66-yard catch-and-run touchdown in the third quarter, pushed his season line to a robust 55-575-7 line across nine games. All three components already are career-high figures, affording Likely massive momentum heading into a Week 11 home showdown against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

short_comment: Skattebo rushed 18 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns and brought in three of four targets for 44 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
long_comment: Skattebo put together an impressive all-around performance that included a season high in receiving yards. He also exceeded the 75-yard mark on the ground for the third time on the campaign, and he went in for his third and fourth rushing touchdowns of the season on one- and 13-yard runs in the first and third quarters, respectively. Skattebo didn't show any ill effects from the hamstring injury that cost him Sunday's win over the Eagles, and he'll now gear up for a Week 11 home matchup against the Jaguars' elite run defense on Sunday, Nov. 22.

short_comment: Pinnock (back) is questionable to return to Thursday night's contest against the Commanders, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Pinnock exited the game early in the third quarter with a back injury, and his status for the rest of the game is uncertain. In his absence, Tyler Nubin will be thrust into a more prominent role in New York's secondary.

short_comment: Carter (knee/back) doesn't have an injury designation for Thursday night's game against the Commanders.
long_comment: Carter logged limited practices Monday and Tuesday before upgrading to full practice Wednesday. Across eight starts this season, the No. 3 overall pick of the 2025 Draft has produced 19 tackles (six solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a forced fumble. He has yet to develop into a game-wrecking edge rusher.

short_comment: Desrosiers carried the ball three times for 20 yards during the Giants' win over the Eagles on Sunday.
long_comment: Desrosiers made his regular-season debut during the victory, serving as the team's No. 2 running back behind Devin Singletary, as Cam Skattebo was out due to a hamstring injury. With Skattebo now healthy again, Desrosiers will likely be relegated to a depth role during Thursday's matchup versus the Commanders.

short_comment: Head coach John Harbaugh told reporters that Hood dislocated his finger during Tuesday's practice, Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post reports.
long_comment: Hood left Tuesday's practice with a trainer after injuring his finger, but Harbaugh told reporters after the session that the rookie second-rounder will "be fine." It's possible that Hood doesn't miss any game time, although Wednesday's injury report will shed light on his status for Thursday's NFC East tilt against the Commanders. Most of his playing time has been on special teams, but Hood's absence would give the Giants less depth in the secondary.

short_comment: Sadiq was limited to a three-yard reception on two targets in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
long_comment: On a day in which quarterbacks Geno Smith (ankle) and Cade Klubnik dropped back 45 times, Sadiq wasn't able to see much involvement in the passing game. Though the rookie first-round pick put his pass-catching chops on display with a 7-105-1 receiving line in Week 3 against Detroit, he's since delivered a collective 10-95-0 line on 19 targets over the Jets' ensuing seven contests. A lack of extended playing time has been a factor in Sadiq's listless production of late; he's logged fewer than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in five of those seven games while second-year tight end Mason Taylor has typically handled larger snap shares.

short_comment: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Cooper (ankle) will undergo imaging Monday, Eric Allen of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Cooper played just one snap before exiting Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills after injuring his right ankle. Notably, the rookie first-round pick tweaked the same ankle in the Jets' Week 1 win over the Titans and was diagnosed with a high-ankle sprain, which resulted in a stint on injured reserve. The Jets are hoping that Cooper avoided as significant of an injury this time around, though even if his imaging yields good news, he could still be hard-pressed to suit up next Sunday versus the Chargers.

short_comment: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Smith will get further imaging on his left ankle Monday, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
long_comment: Glenn said that he won't have an update on Smith's status until later in the week once his MRI results are read, but the coach noted that Smith -- if healthy -- will remain the Jets' starting quarterback heading into next Sunday's game against the Chargers. Smith played less than half of the Jets' offensive snaps in this past Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills, missing time while getting checked for a concussion and then due to the ankle injury. Backup Cade Klubnik finished out the game under center in place of Smith, who completed 13 of 21 throws for 148 yards before exiting for good in the third quarter.

short_comment: Mitchell caught three passes for 59 yards on eight targets in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
long_comment: With Garrett Wilson back from his one-game absence Sunday, Mitchell was left fighting for secondary looks. His eight targets were second on the team, trailing Wilson's 14, and Omar Cooper's early-game ankle injury helped Mitchell's volume solidify. If Cooper is going to miss time going forward, Mitchell will be a more comfortable fantasy WR3 play with upside headed into next Sunday's game against the Chargers.

short_comment: Allen rushed eight times for 40 yards and caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
long_comment: For a second consecutive game, Allen was outplayed by Breece Hall, who produced 108 scrimmage yards on 15 touches. Allen remains the more efficient runner, averaging 5.0 yards per carry to Hall's 3.4 this season, but Hall is the team's preferred option in passing situations, which have been plentiful with the 2-8 Jets frequently in catch-up mode. Perhaps a Week 11 matchup with a Chargers team that's still searching for its first win through Sunday of Week 10 will offer an opportunity to stick with the run and play to Allen's strengths.

short_comment: Klubnik completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. He added three rushing attempts for 26 yards.
long_comment: Klubnik saw the first regular-season action of his NFL career in the second half of Sunday's loss, as Geno Smith (ankle) exited the game. The rookie fourth-round pick led the offense down to Buffalo's four-yard line on his first possession in the third quarter, but the Jets settled for a field goal on that possession, and Klubnik was picked off on his next drive. If Smith isn't ready to return in Week 11, Klubnik would be in line to make his first regular-season start on the road against the Chargers.

short_comment: Hall rushed 11 times for 41 yards and caught all four of his targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
long_comment: Hall narrowly topped Braelon Allen (eight carries for 40 yards) for the team lead in rushing yards and finished second behind Garrett Wilson (seven catches for 106 yards) in both receptions and receiving yards. While Allen continues to be more efficient as a rusher, Hall's superior receiving ability should help the latter maintain the edge in playing time for a 2-8 Jets team that often finds itself playing catch-up. Rookie QB Cade Klubnik, who played most of the second half Sunday, could be more reliant on check downs to Hall than veteran Geno Smith (ankle) was, but it remains to be seen who will get the nod under center in Week 11 against the Chargers.

short_comment: Wilson (concussion) caught seven of 14 targets for 106 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
long_comment: Wilson set a new season high in targets and came one yard short of his Week 3 season high Sunday in his return from a one-game absence due to a concussion. His production came on a mix of passes from Geno Smith (ankle) and rookie Cade Klubnik, the latter of whom saw his first NFL action after Smith exited in the second half. Wilson figures to work as the top target for whomever starts under center in a Week 11 road game against the Chargers.

short_comment: Parham (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Bills.
long_comment: Parham exited the second quarter of Sunday's game with a knee injury. Jordan Meredith is set to fill in at left guard while Parham is absent.

short_comment: Payne (knee) is active for Sunday's game against Buffalo.
long_comment: Payne missed the Jets' first nine games of the regular season while on injured reserve due to a bone bruise in his knee. He was activated from IR on Saturday, and the rookie seventh-rounder was given the green light to make his NFL regular-season debut in Week 10.

short_comment: Wright (back) is active for Sunday's game against the Bills.
long_comment: Wright was cleared by medical staff to return from a one-game absence due to a back injury. His return gives the Jets another contributor on special teams and extra depth in the secondary.

short_comment: Ossai (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Bills.
long_comment: Ossai missed the Jets' last four games while recovering from an ankle injury, but the sixth-year pro was cleared by medical staff to return for Sunday's AFC East tilt. He logged nine tackles (five solo) across three regular-season games prior to his injury.

short_comment: Phillips (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Bills.
long_comment: Phillips was trending in the right direction to play Sunday after logging a full practice Friday. The veteran defensive tackle was cleared to suit up after going through pregame warmups, and he'll face the team that drafted him in the third round of the 2018 NFL Draft. Phillips has 26 tackles (seven solo) and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Bailey tallied nine tackles (five solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two forced fumbles during the Jets' loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
long_comment: Bailey had a productive outing despite the loss as he was the only Jets defender to record a sack. The 23-year-old has gotten off to a strong start during his rookie campaign, compiling 34 tackles (26 solo), including 7.5 sacks, and five forced fumbles across his first eight games.

short_comment: Williams did not draw a target in Sunday's Week 9 loss to Kansas City. However, he rushed once for four yards, returned one punt for 18 yards and returned two kickoffs for 55 yards.
long_comment: Williams didn't get a ball thrown his way despite logging a 60 percent offensive snap share. While the Illinois product continues to have a role in multiple facets of the game for New York, he's not making much of an impact as a pass catcher. Williams has one or zero catches in five straight contests and has tallied only 34 receiving yards during that span.

short_comment: Taylor recorded one catch for 11 yards on two targets in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
long_comment: Even with Garrett Wilson (concussion) inactive, Taylor's two targets were his fewest in a game since Week 2, and he left that one early with a thumb injury. It was Kenyon Sadiq who had Geno Smith's eyes against Kansas City, as the rookie tight end recorded four grabs for 49 yards on four targets. Taylor is more of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option at the position.

short_comment: Davis didn't play any offensive snaps in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
long_comment: With Breece Hall back from his quad injury to form a backfield duo with Braelon Allen, Davis was relegated to RB3 duties and played 16 snaps on special teams. Davis has rushed 15 times for 44 yards, while recording five grabs for 68 yards on six targets across nine appearances this season.

short_comment: The Jets signed Reeder to their active roster Monday, Amanda Vogt of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Reeder is returning to New York after having been released by the Jets in October. The 32-year-old has logged four tackles (one solo) across six outings this season and will likely continue to see the majority of his playing time come on special teams during his second tenure with the Jets.

short_comment: McDonald put in a request for the Jets to trade him ahead of Tuesday's deadline, Ian Rapoport and Rich Cimini of ESPN report.
long_comment: The 2023 first-round pick racked up 18.5 sacks over the previous two seasons and has three on his ledger through nine games in 2026, but he's seen his playing time tail off with the arrival of No. 2 overall pick David Bailey and the addition of Kingsley Enagbare in free agency. Though McDonald is hopeful to land with a team that can present him with a clearer path to a full-time role, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Monday that McDonald "is going to be here" once the deadline passes, per Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic.

short_comment: The Eagles opened Shipley's (foot) 21-day practice window Monday.
long_comment: Shipley landed on IR after being diagnosed with a partial tear of his plantar fascia in the wake of Week 5 action, but now has a chance to play as soon as Sunday against the Steelers. Meanwhile, fellow RB Tank Bigsby (abdomen) -- who hasn't played since Week 4 -- remains on IR, and the Eagles signed Jaydon Blue to their practice squad Monday. If he's able to suit up this weekend, Shipley would reclaim a backup role behind Saquon Barkley that isn't likely to result in much volume for the 2024 fourth-rounder.

short_comment: The Eagles signed Ertz from the practice squad to the active roster Monday.
long_comment: Philadelphia is coming off a Week 10 bye, but prior to the midseason respite, there were no reported injuries in the TE group on the active roster. When the position group was depleted earlier this season, the team used elevations on Ertz from Weeks 3-5, but his snap share decreased game by game (38, 21 and 11 percent), while he hauled in three of eight targets for 22 yards in that span. Wednesday's practice report will reveal if any of Dallas Goedert, Eli Stowers, Johnny Mundt or Grant Calcaterra are banged up at the moment.

short_comment: Trotter recorded 11 tackles (five solo) and one forced fumble during the Eagles' 19-11 loss to the Giants in Week 9.
long_comment: Trotter was on the field for 64 of the Eagles' 67 defensive snaps (95.5 percent), and he was the only Philadelphia defender to reach double-digit stops. He's tallied at least 10 tackles three times in 2026, and the third-year pro is up to 51 tackles (32 solo), including 0.5 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Moore caught one of two targets for minus-3 yards during the Eagles' 19-11 loss to the Giants on Sunday.
long_comment: Week 9 was the Eagles' first game with Joe Milton as the starter, with Tanner McKee relegated to backup duties. Milton completed 18 of his 34 passes, and his lone connection with Moore resulted in a three-yard loss. The Eagles are on a bye for Week 10, and Moore's role on the offense would evaporate if one or both of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) or Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was cleared to play in Week 11 against the Steelers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

short_comment: Cooper caught just two of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
long_comment: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) still out, Cooper played more than 90 percent of the offensive snaps for the third straight game. He's done very little with that playing time, producing five catches for 61 yards during that span. Cooper is well off the fantasy radar until he shows something in the box score, and that's if Smith and Wicks remain sidelined.

short_comment: Ebiketie will remain with the Eagles after his reported trade to the Bengals on Tuesday fell through and won't be completed, according to NFL reporter Jordan Schultz.
long_comment: Earlier Tuesday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network relayed that the Eagles agreed to send Ebiketie to the Bengals in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick. The trade wasn't cancelled due to concerns over Ebiketie's physical; instead, the Bengals opted to call it off since they would have lost a third-round compensatory pick if the deal was completed, per Rapoport. The Eagles could still look to move Ebiketie elsewhere prior to Tuesday's deadline, but barring another trade, he'll suit up for Philadelphia in its Week 10 game against Pittsburgh.

short_comment: Mitchell reverted to the Eagles' practice squad Monday.
long_comment: Mitchell has been elevated each of the past three weeks and has logged at least six touches in every game during that span. During this past Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants, he recorded six yards on three carries and caught three passes for 20 yards on four targets. The Eagles would need to sign Mitchell to the 53-man roster in order for him to be eligible to play in their next game, which will be Nov. 22 versus Pittsburgh following a Week 10 bye. That opportunity for Mitchell could depend on whether Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and/or Will Shipley (foot) return from injured reserve.

short_comment: Elliott made his lone field-goal attempt in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
long_comment: Elliott's kick was good from 45 yards, but with Joe Milton making his first start at quarterback and without DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), the Philly offense struggled to move the ball and score points. Elliott is not an exciting fantasy kicker on a tanking Eagles team.

short_comment: Stowers failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
long_comment: The rookie tight end ran just four routes on Joe Milton's 48 dropbacks against the G-Men. Grant Calcaterra ran just six, as the Eagles used more three-wide sets than multiple TE sets. Stowers would need a Dallas Goedert injury or trade to come into any fantasy value.
