short_comment: Lemon caught six of nine targets for 61 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
long_comment: Lemon showed a nice rapport with QB Joe Milton in Milton's first NFL start, as the rookie first-round pick led the Eagles in catches, receiving yards and targets. Lemon has operated as Philadelphia's de facto No. 1 WR while DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) have both missed the past three games, but the Eagles could get at least one of their top two wideouts back in Week 11 against the Steelers following a Week 10 bye.

short_comment: Goedert caught five of six targets for 50 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
long_comment: Goedert finished one catch and 11 yards shy of Makai Lemon's team-leading totals in Joe Milton's first start for the Eagles. Both of Goedert's touchdowns this season came back in Week 1, and the Eagles have since changed QBs twice. Goedert's best result in the three games started by Tanner McKee was a six-catch, 61-yard outing, so the veteran TE has remained consistent even as the offense around him falls apart due to injuries. Milton, McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton are all potential candidates to start in Week 11 against the Steelers after Philadelphia's Week 10 bye.

short_comment: Milton completed 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants. He also rushed nine times for 64 yards, ran in a two-point conversion and lost a fumble.
long_comment: The big-armed Milton wasn't effective as a passer while working with a depleted receiving corps that was missing DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), but Milton showcased strong mobility and led the Eagles in rushing yards while RBs Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell combined for just 28 rushing yards on 16 carries. The 2024 sixth-round pick of the Patriots played nearly the full game in the 2024 regular-season finale against the Bills and got into four games with Dallas during the 2025 campaign, but this was Milton's first regular-season NFL start. Philadelphia's Week 10 bye will provide an opportunity to evaluate a QB room consisting of Milton, the recently benched Tanner McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton. Whichever QB gets the starting nod in Week 11 against the Steelers would benefit from the potential return of Smith or Wicks after the bye.

short_comment: Barkley rushed 13 times for 22 yards and a touchdown while failing to catch his only target in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
long_comment: Barkley has mustered a meager 2.0 yards per carry over the past two games while playing through hamstring and back injuries, but he also has both of Philadelphia's touchdowns over that span, including a three-yard rushing score in the second quarter Sunday. It has been a slog offensively for the Eagles, who have tried first Tanner McKee and now Joe Milton under center since losing starting QB Jalen Hurts (IR, calf) likely for the season while also playing without top two wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). It's fair to wonder if Barkley will eventually be shut down as well to get a chance to heal as the 2-7 Eagles drop out of contention, but at least a Week 10 bye will offer him a respite before Philadelphia's Week 11 home game against the Steelers.

short_comment: Baun (back) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Giants.
long_comment: Baun exited the second half of Sunday's game with a back injury. Smael Mondon will fill in at inside linebacker opposite Jeremiah Trotter while Baun receives further medical evaluation to determine if he can return to the contest.

short_comment: McKee (ribs) is active for Sunday's game against the Giants.
long_comment: McKee has overcome his rib injury in time to suit up for Sunday's contest. The quarterback is set to back up Joe Milton against the Giants due to the absence of former starter Jalen Hurts (calf, IR).

short_comment: Could Mike McCarthy said Monday that the Steelers are 'hopeful' they can get Pittman -- who last played in Week 4 -- back from his foot injury this week, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
long_comment: The same goes for Roman Wilson (finger), who saw his last game action in Week 5. In the duo's absence, DK Metcalf has led Pittsburgh's WR corps, with Germie Bernard having seen his role expand in the process. Prior to his injury, Pittman caught seven of his 12 targets for 89 yards in three games, but once he rejoins the lineup, the 29-year-old -- who had at least 111 targets in each of his last five seasons with the Colts -- could resurface on the fantasy radar in PPR formats.

short_comment: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said that he's "hopeful" Wilson (finger) will be able to return from injured reserve for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
long_comment: Now that he's spent the required four games on IR while recovering from a finger injury, Wilson is eligible to have his 21-day practice window opened this week. McCarthy expressed similar optimism that fellow wideout Michael Pittman (foot) will be able to come off IR this week, a development that could result in Wilson settling for a lesser role if both receivers are activated ahead of Sunday's contest. Despite a rough start to the season, Pittman signed a two-year, $35 million extension in March that likely affords him some security as a starter alongside DK Metcalf upon his return, which would leave Wilson to fend with rookie second-round pick Germie Bernard for the No. 3 spot on the depth chart.

short_comment: Rudolph completed one of three pass attempts for two yards and rushed once for nine yards in Sunday's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
long_comment: After the Bengals had built a 20-point lead with five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, head coach Mike McCarthy opted to remove starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers from the game and turned to Rudolph to direct the offense for the Steelers' final possession. Rudolph led the Steelers on an 11-play drive that concluded in the red zone before time expired. The 31-year-old Rudolph has now made four relief appearances behind Rodgers on the season, playing limited snaps in each of those contests.

short_comment: Metcalf brought in two of six targets for 54 yards and a touchdown and added a two-point conversion catch in the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday night.
long_comment: Metcalf's yardage total, modest as it was, led the Steelers on the night. The veteran receiver got there with the help of a team-long 32-yard catch, while his other reception was a 22-yard scoring grab early in the fourth quarter that Metcalf followed up with a two-point conversion. Metcalf has at least Sunday night's yardage total in three of the last four games, but he's still sporting an inefficient 35-432-2 line on 70 targets through nine games heading into a Week 11 road matchup against the Eagles next Sunday.

short_comment: Warren rushed seven times for 15 yards and brought in five of six targets for 26 yards in the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday night. He committed a fumble recovered by Pittsburgh.
long_comment: The Steelers were quickly dissuaded from a balanced offensive approach when the Bengals accumulated 24 first-half points, leading to Warren's lowest carry and rushing yardage totals of the season. Warren did tie his second-highest reception total of the campaign thanks in part to how the game unfolded, but it was ultimately a nearly irrelevant fantasy night relative to the lofty standards the versatile back has set this season. Warren will look to get back on track at the expense of the struggling Eagles in a Week 11 intrastate road showdown next Sunday.

short_comment: Dowdle rushed five times for 26 yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards during Sunday's 38-18 defeat at Cincinnati.
long_comment: Dowdle's previous low-water mark in touches was nine in Week 2 at New England, and on the season he averaged 11.8 touches per game entering Week 10 action. As a result, he finished with his second-fewest yards from scrimmage (34) in a contest this season, while backfield mate Jaylen Warren (12 touches for 41 total yards) also found little success in any facet. Dowdle remains the No. 2 RB in Pittsburgh behind Warren and thus is a hit-or-miss option in a Week 11 road matchup with the Eagles next Sunday.

short_comment: Freiermuth recorded two catches (on three targets) for 35 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 38-18 loss in Cincinnati.
long_comment: Freiermuth was added to the Steelers' injury report Saturday due to an illness that left him questionable for Week 10 action. Ultimately, he avoided inactive status and also made an end-zone visit for the first time since Week 5 on a 27-yard hookup with QB Aaron Rodgers in the fourth quarter. Considering Freiermuth hasn't reached 50 receiving yards in any game this season, he remains a TD-dependent fantasy option (five in his nine appearances).

short_comment: Rodgers completed 15 of 29 passes for 143 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed two times for minus-1 yard during Sunday's 38-18 loss at Cincinnati.
long_comment: The Steelers sat at 33 total yards of offense after three quarters, so the vast majority of Rodgers' output occurred on the team's three fourth-quarter possessions, two of which ended in touchdown connections with WR DK Metcalf (22 yards) and TE Pat Freiermuth (27 yards). Through nine games this season, Rodgers has tossed multiple TDs on five occasions, but he's also been held to less than 200 yards through the air three times. Rodgers will seek better results next Sunday in Phildadelphia.

short_comment: McCormick suffered an ankle injury in Sunday night's game against the Bengals and will not return, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
long_comment: The Steelers' left guard went down toward the end of the first half and was immediately placed in an air cast and carted off the field, suggesting this is a long-term injury for the third-year lineman. Spencer Anderson will handle left-guard duties for Pittsburgh the remainder of Sunday night's game.

short_comment: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive and serving as Pittsburgh's emergency third quarterback Sunday night versus Cincinnati.
long_comment: Howard has regularly worked in the emergency third-quarterback role this season, though it has yet to result in any game action. He'll be eligible to enter the matchup Sunday night only if both Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

short_comment: Harmon (foot) is active for Sunday's Week 10 clash against Cincinnati.
long_comment: Harmon landed on IR in early October due to a foot injury. He was designated to return this past Wednesday and logged an LP/LP/FP practice progression this week. Harmon is now set to return to the field Sunday night, though it's unclear if he'll be eased back into action in terms of defensive snap share.

short_comment: Elliott suffered a pregame knee injury and has been ruled out for Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Bengals.
long_comment: Elliott dealt with an ankle issue during Week 10 prep but was initially cleared to suit up Sunday. However, he's now dealing with a knee injury that occurred during pregame warmups. Elliott's loss is a blow to Pittsburgh's secondary, though he's played in only two games so far this season. Robert Spears-Jennings figures to take on a large defensive snap share Sunday in Elliott's stead.

short_comment: Echols (hamstring) was a full participant at practice Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
long_comment: Echols missed the last two games before Pittsburgh's bye in Week 9 because of a hamstring injury, but it looks like he's on track to be available in Week 10. Through six games so far in 2026, a substantial majority of his snaps have come on special teams.

short_comment: Slaughter (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
long_comment: Slaughter was unable to play against the Browns in Week 8 due to a hamstring injury that prevented him from practicing. His ability to log a full session Wednesday puts him on track to play against the Bengals on Sunday, when he's expected to play mostly on special teams while providing the Steelers depth in the secondary.

short_comment: Skowronek (calf) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
long_comment: Skowronek was sidelined by a calf injury for the Steelers' three games prior to the Week 9 bye. His full practice participation Wednesday indicates that he is fully recovered from the injury and will suit up for Sunday's contest against the Browns. Skowronek has three catches on four targets for 32 yards and a touchdown across five regular-season games.

short_comment: Boswell made two of his three field-goal attempts and all three PATs in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.
long_comment: Boswell missed a 57-yard attempt on the Steelers' first offensive drive of the game. The kicker proceeded to nail 20-yard and 37-yard attempts en route to five straight made kicks. Boswell is now 18-for-23 on field-goal attempts and 16-for-16 on PATs through eight regular-season games in 2026.

short_comment: Bernard caught all five of his targets for 30 yards during Sunday's 27-6 win against Cleveland.
long_comment: Bernard led the team in catches, reeling in multiple passes for the fifth straight week and sixth time overall this year. The wide receiver has built a strong rapport with starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers, but it's unclear what Bernard's workload will look like after the Steelers have a chance to regroup and potentially acquire another pass catcher during the team's bye week in Week 9.

short_comment: Washington caught three of five targets for 94 yards during Sunday's 27-6 win over the Browns.
long_comment: Washington led the team in receiving yards while finishing tied for second on the team in targets with wide receiver Germie Bernard. The tight end's biggest moment of the game came in the third quarter when he reeled in a short pass from Aaron Rodgers and took off for a 58-yard gain. Washington has corralled 19 of 28 targets for 254 yards and three touchdowns over eight contests to open the 2026 regular season.

short_comment: The Steelers signed Smith off the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Smith had already been elevated from the practice squad thrice, so Saturday's move means he's eligible to suit up for the Steelers for the rest of the season. The Iowa product caught both of his targets for 24 yards against the Saints in Week 7. If Ben Skowronek (calf) cannot play Sunday, then Smith, Kaden Wetjen and Brandon Johnson would all be in line for more offensive snaps.

short_comment: Wilson totaled six tackles (three solo) and an interception during Pittsburgh's win over the Saints on Sunday.
long_comment: Wilson had a solid outing in the win, as he recorded the team's lone interception of Tyler Shough. The 26-year-old has now compiled 61 tackles (33 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and an interception across the first seven games of the campaign. He will look to keep producing during next week's matchup against the Browns.

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday that the 49ers are "hoping to" have Evans (Achilles) back at practice this week, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: After missing the 49ers' last three games while recovering from right Achilles tendinitis, Evans looks to have a chance at returning to action in Week 11. After staying behind in the Bay Area this past weekend for the 49ers' 46-40 win in Dallas, Evans is scheduled to meet back up with the 49ers this week in Colorado Springs, where the team will be holding practices at high altitude to get acclimated for Sunday's matchup with the Vikings in Mexico City. If Evans is able to practice in some capacity Wednesday through Friday and if his Achilles responds well, he'll likely be cleared for his first game action since Week 6.

short_comment: Allen brought in five of seven targets for 61 yards in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.
long_comment: Allen looked rejuvenated in his 49ers debut after coming over from the Colts at the deadline, finishing third in receptions and receiving yards and second in targets for his new squad in the wild win. Allen and Brock Purdy seemed to have instant chemistry despite having practiced on only three occasions coming into the contest, and the veteran receiver's production should have a good chance of spiking further down the stretch of the regular season.

short_comment: Kittle brought in six of nine targets for 74 yards in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.
long_comment: Kittle put together a very solid fantasy performance that was easily lost in the shuffle of multiple spectacular efforts by players on either side. However, the veteran tight end did pace the 49ers in receptions and targets while finishing second in receiving yards, and he's now recorded at least 70 yards on five occasions this season. Kittle is up to a 44-557-5 line on 62 targets through nine games as a Week 11 home showdown against the Vikings next Sunday night approaches.

short_comment: Samuel rushed three times for 78 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for 31 yards and another score in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.
long_comment: Samuel made his return from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury, and the versatile veteran was put right to work as the de facto No. 1 receiver with Mike Evans (Achilles) still sidelined. Samuel came just a yard short of tying his single-game career high in rushing yards, and his receiving and rushing touchdowns came from 11 and 70 yards out, respectively. Samuel has five total touchdowns through six games heading into a Week 11 home matchup against a tough Vikings defense next Sunday night.

short_comment: Purdy completed 22 of 28 passes for 389 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions and added two carries for 21 yards in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday. He also threw a two-point conversion pass.
long_comment: As expected, Sunday's showdown between the longtime rivals turned into a complete offensive showcase, and Purdy was right at the center of the fireworks. The veteran quarterback recorded a career-high passing yardage total, with his 66-yard touchdown pass to Christian McCaffrey with just over three minutes remaining putting Purdy over the top. That TD toss was preceded by 11- and 74-yard scoring strikes to Deebo Samuel and McCaffrey, respectively, in the first half, giving Purdy his third tally of at least three touchdown passes this season. Purdy's 78.6 percent completion rate also was his second-highest total of the season, and the fact the star signal-caller seemed to have quick chemistry with trade-deadline acquisition Keenan Allen bodes very well, considering Purdy also may have Mike Evans (Achilles) back for next Sunday night's Week 11 home showdown against the Vikings.

short_comment: McCaffrey rushed 13 times for 62 yards and a touchdown and brought in all four targets for 161 yards and two more scores in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday. He also caught a two-point conversion pass.
long_comment: While McCaffrey's touches once again were kept below 20, the elite running back finished with a season-high total in yards from scrimmage with a career-best performance as a receiver. He struck first through the air, recording a 74-yard touchdown reception late in the first half. The versatile veteran then went in on the ground from 16 yards out early in the fourth quarter to extend San Francisco's lead to 38-19 at the time, before sealing the extremely hard-fought victory with a spectacular 66-yard catch-and-run TD on a slant and an ensuing two-point conversion grab with just over three minutes remaining after the Cowboys had closed to 38-32. McCaffrey has a relatively modest-by-his-standards 155 touches over nine games, but he's still just 50 yards short of 1,000 total yards for the season heading into next Sunday night's Week 11 home showdown against the Vikings.

short_comment: Black rushed 11 times for 53 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 46-40 win over the Cowboys. He added two catches for 13 yards on two targets.
long_comment: The rookie running back has tallied double-digit carries in three straight games and played 26 of 65 offensive snaps behind Christian McCaffrey's 39 snaps. CMC was also extremely productive out of the backfield against Dallas' Swiss-cheese defense, turning 17 touches into 243 total yards and three touchdowns. Black is more involved than most of McCaffrey's backups have been in recent seasons, and the rookie is offering some standalone RB2/3 valuation in one of the league's most efficient offenses. Over the last three games, Black has rushed 34 times for 186 yards (5.5 YPC) and two touchdowns.

short_comment: Williams (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
long_comment: Williams' practice reps during Week 10 prep were limited due to a shoulder injury. However, the veteran left tackle was given the green light to play after going through pregame warmups.

short_comment: Lenoir (foot) is active for Sunday's game against Dallas.
long_comment: Lenoir earned the questionable tag for Week 10 after logging a limited practice Friday, and he's been cleared by medical staff to play Sunday after going through pregame warmups. He's been working through a foot injury that he picked up during the 49ers' 38-17 win over the Raiders in Week 9.

short_comment: Greenlaw (knee) is active for Sunday's game against Dallas.
long_comment: Greenlaw injured his knee during Thursday's practice session and was deemed questionable for Week 10, but the veteran linebacker has been cleared by medical staff to play in Sunday's contest. He has 57 tackles (27 solo), one forced fumble and one fumble recovery through seven regular-season games.

short_comment: Cooks (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
long_comment: Mike Evans (Achilles) is also inactive for a third consecutive game, but Cooks' services are not needed Sunday due to the return of Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and the acquisition of Keenan Allen from the Colts on Tuesday. It's unclear if Cooks will have any role in the 49ers' offense once Evans is cleared to return. For now, Cooks' next chance to suit up is Week 11 against the Vikings on Nov. 22.

short_comment: West (knee) won't be activated from IR ahead of Sunday's Week 10 clash against the Cowboys, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
long_comment: West has been on IR since Sept. 23 due to a knee injury. He upgraded to a full practice session Friday after being limited Wednesday and Thursday, but the 49ers aren't yet ready to activate him. Prior to getting hurt, West logged action in two games, recording five tackles (one solo) over 49 defensive snaps and five special-teams snaps.

short_comment: The 49ers aren't activating Hobbs (adductor) ahead of Sunday's tilt against Dallas, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
long_comment: Hobbs had his 21-day practice window opened Nov. 4, so the 49ers still have ample time to activate him before he'd need to miss the rest of the season. The veteran cornerback hasn't yet made his regular-season San Francisco debut after signing with the team on a one-year contract last March. Hobbs did manage to log a trio of full practices this week, so he seems to be progressing well toward a return to action.

short_comment: Halton recently underwent surgery to repair a broken leg and dislocated ankle that he suffered during the 49ers' Week 9 win over the Raiders, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
long_comment: Halton will be sidelined for the rest of the 2026 season, but the rookie fourth-rounder is expected to be back for OTAs in May. He'll end his first NFL campaign with 15 tackles (nine solo), including 2.0 sacks, one pass defense and a scoop-and-score across eight regular-season games.

short_comment: Dugger recorded six solo tackles and a pick-six during the 49ers' 38-17 win over the Raiders in Week 9.
long_comment: Dugger set the tone for the 49ers right out of halftime, when he intercepted a pass from Kirk Cousins intended for Tre Tucker and returned it 35 yards for a pick-six for the first defensive touchdown of Dugger's young NFL career. The rookie fifth-rounder has logged at least six solo tackles in three of his last four games and is up to 36 tackles (25 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pick-six through eight regular-season games.

short_comment: Warner logged five tackles (three solo), one forced fumble and one fumble recovery during the 49ers' 38-17 win over the Raiders in Week 9.
long_comment: Warner's five stops tied a season low, although he did recover the fumble late in the third quarter that the 49ers' offense converted into a 37-yard touchdown pass from Brock Purdy to Jordan Watkins seven plays later. Warner has played every single defensive snap in each of the 49ers' last six games, and the veteran linebacker is up to 77 tackles (36 solo), including 0.5 sacks, three pass defenses, five forced fumbles and one fumble recovery through eight regular-season games.

short_comment: Robinson caught three passes for 22 yards on four targets in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.
long_comment: Playing in his first game since Week 2 due to a high ankle sprain, Robinson played 51 percent of the Niners' offensive snaps against Las Vegas. San Francisco's wideout situation is a week-to-week thing moving forward, with the Tuesday addition of Keenan Allen and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Mike Evans (Achilles) and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) all likely to return at some point in the near future. Robinson isn't someone to roster in 12-team fantasy leagues.

short_comment: The 49ers fielded trade inquiries for Jones from the Vikings leading up to Tuesday's deadline, but the quarterback is expected to remain in San Francisco, Dianna Russini of BetUS TV reports.
long_comment: Even though starting quarterback Brock Purdy has been a leading MVP candidate through the halfway point of the season, the 49ers still place a premium value on Jones as an insurance option in the event Purdy misses time due to injury. As such, the 49ers' asking price for Jones was too rich for the Vikings, who have since pivoted their focus to acquiring Kirk Cousins from the Raiders.

short_comment: James rushed three times for 11 yards and returned two kickoffs for 31 yards Sunday in a 38-17 victory versus Las Vegas.
long_comment: As has been the case all season, James filled a minor role in San Francisco's backfield behind Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black. James' three touches Sunday were his second most this season behind the four touches he logged in Week 2 versus Miami. James likely will be relegated to making most of his impact as a returner unless either McCaffrey or Black misses time.

short_comment: Head coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that he's "really optimistic" Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) will be able to get a full week's worth of practice coming out of the Seahawks' Week 11 bye and start their next game Nov. 29 against the 49ers, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Darnold, who last played Week 8, is still working his way through a pair of injuries, but barring any setbacks, he's trending toward a Week 12 return. Macdonald reiterated that Darnold will be the team's starter once healthy, even though backup Drew Lock has guided Seattle to a 4-0 record while coming on in relief or starting in place of an injured Darnold in the first two games of the season as well as the most recent two contests.

short_comment: Barner caught all three targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.
long_comment: Barner has been held below 25 receiving yards in eight of 10 games this season and has more rushing touchdowns (two) than receiving scores (one) during the 2026 campaign. He's the definition of a low-floor, touchdown-or-bust fantasy option headed into the team's bye week.

short_comment: Shaheed caught one pass for eight yards on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.
long_comment: After missing the previous two games with a knee injury, Shaheed returned against Las Vegas and maintained his role as the WR3 for Seattle. He played 25 of 57 offensive snaps and remained a non-factor in the box score. Shaheed has yet to hit 70 receiving yards in a game this season and has zero touchdowns as a pass catcher. He's off the fantasy radar.

short_comment: Lock completed 14 of 17 passes for 240 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions and logged six carries for 20 yards during Sunday's 21-13 victory in Las Vegas.
long_comment: Lock took advantage of having WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba at his disposal, targeting him 10 times, one of which resulted in a 71-yard TD connection. Moreover, Lock also hooked up with Cooper Kupp on a sliding 34-yard touchdown, marking his second multi-TD outing in four appearances (three starts) this season. There's an expectation that Seahawks No. 1 QB Sam Darnold (quadriceps) returns from a two-game absence after the team's Week 11 bye, but until he receives a clean bill of health, Lock has a chance to be under center on the road against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Price posted nine carries for 36 yards and one touchdown and gathered in his only target for eight yards during Sunday's 21-13 victory at Las Vegas.
long_comment: This marks Price's fewest touches in a game since returning from IR in Week 8, and he actually was doubled up in the category by position mate Zach Charbonnet, who turned his 20 rushes into 94 yards. Having said that, Price salvaged his day with a 12-yard TD, the first of his career, on the ground in the third quarter. The breakdown of work between the two may signal what's to come in the Seahawks backfield after the team's Week 11 bye, with Price and company set to face off with the NFC West-leading 49ers on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Charbonnet churned out 94 yards on 20 carries during Sunday's 21-13 win in Las Vegas.
long_comment: Charbonnet was eased in to the mix in Weeks 8 and 9, going from nine touches in the first contest to 17 in the latter. This time around, though, he doubled up fellow RB Jadarian Price in touches (10) and more than did so in terms from yards from scrimmage (44). It may signal that Charbonnet is the Seahawks' clear-cut No. 1 backfield option moving forward, but he won't have a chance to prove as much until after the team's Week 11 bye on Sunday, Nov. 29, at San Francisco.

short_comment: Smith-Njigba gathered in eight of 10 targets for 171 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 21-13 win at Las Vegas.
long_comment: Smith-Njigba's Week 10 performance was fueled by a 71-yard catch and run for a touchdown in the middle of the third quarter, but he still was able to put up 100 yards on his other seven receptions en route to a new season high in the category. As the Seahawks hit their Week 11 bye, he's reached the century mark in receiving eight times and resides on a 79-1,207-10 line on 109 targets through 10 contests. Smith-Njigba's next chance to continue aggravating opposing defenses arrives Sunday, Nov. 29, at San Francisco.

short_comment: Reed is doubtful to return to Sunday's game against Las Vegas due to a toe injury.
long_comment: Reed limped off the field during the first half and was subsequently deemed doubtful to return. Brandon Pili should get a lot more defensive snaps in the likely scenario that Reed is unable to re-enter Sunday's contest.

short_comment: Lucas (ankle) is doubtful to return to Sunday's game against the Raiders.
long_comment: Lucas exited the first quarter of Sunday's game with an ankle injury. The right tackle appears to have sustained a significant injury and likely will not return to the contest. Josh Jones should finish the game at right tackle for the Seahawks.

short_comment: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game at Arizona.
long_comment: Since Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned to the lineup in Week 8 against the Bears, Wilson was contained to special teams in that contest and then was active but didn't log a snap last Sunday versus the Cardinals. Now, Wilson will yield all the RB reps to Charbonnet, Price and George Holani in Week 10.

short_comment: Pili (back) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
long_comment: Pili missed the Seahawks' last two games while nursing a back injury, but he's been cleared to play in Week 10 after logging a full practice session Friday. His return gives the Seahawks more depth on the interior defensive line behind Byron Murphy.

short_comment: Nwosu (ankle) does not have an injury designation against the Raiders on Sunday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
long_comment: Nwosu has missed the Seahawks' last two games while tending to an ankle injury, but he's been cleared to play Sunday after ending Week 10 prep with a full practice Friday. His return means less defensive snaps will be available for Derick Hall, Dante Fowler and Connor O'Toole.

short_comment: Hall (back) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
long_comment: Hall was limited in each of the first two practices of Week 10 prep before sitting out Friday's session. However, his reduced practice reps appear to have been planned by the Seahawks to manage his back injury, and the fourth-year pro has been given the green light to play in Sunday's contest. Hall has 24 tackles (14 solo), including 3.0 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Jones tallied seven tackles (three solo) during Seattle's win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: Jones finished tied for second on the team in tackles behind Julian Love during Sunday's victory. Jones has now racked up seven or more tackles in all nine of his outings to start the season and will look to keep producing next week versus the Raiders.

short_comment: Kupp caught three of four targets for 32 yards during the Seahawks' 17-3 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: All three of Kupp's catches came on the same offensive drive midway through the third quarter, which ended with a 45-yard field goal by Jason Myers. The Seahawks had Drew Lock under center due to the absence of Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs), but Lock is now dealing with an oblique injury that could prevent him from playing in Week 10 against the Raiders on Nov. 15. Jalen Milroe would be the next man up at quarterback for Seattle, which would lower the floors for Kupp and the rest of the Seahawks' pass catchers. Kupp has a 22-238-2 receiving line on 34 targets through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Horton caught two passes for 22 yards on three targets in Sunday's 17-3 win over the Cardinals.
long_comment: Horton has just seven catches for 67 yards across six games since Week 3. The Seahawks' No. 3 receiver is well off the fantasy radar, even with Rashid Shaheed (knee) injured.

short_comment: The Buccaneers signed Stick off their practice squad Monday, Scott Smith of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Stick has been a member of the Buccaneers' practice squad all season, with Tampa Bay having previously elevated him from Weeks 4 through 6 to back up Jalon Daniels while he filled in as the starter in place of Baker Mayfield, who had been out due to a dislocated thumb. Mayfield has since moved past that injury, but he's currently nursing a sprained foot coming out of the Buccaneers' Week 9 loss to the Bears. Tampa Bay's decision to sign Stick implies some concern about Mayfield's status heading into Sunday's game against the Lions, potentially setting the stage for Stick to back up Daniels for the fourth time this season.

short_comment: Mayfield's availability for next Sunday's game against the Lions is in question due to an injury he sustained to his foot and ankle area during the Buccaneers' Week 9 loss to the Bears, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
long_comment: While Tampa Bay has been on bye for Week 10, Mayfield has been in and out of a walking boot in recent days in an attempt to rehab the injury, per Garafolo. Though the injury isn't viewed as a long-term concern and a stint on injured reserve isn't in consideration, Mayfield could still be at risk of missing his fourth game of the season in Week 11, after he was sidelined from Weeks 4 through 6 due to a dislocated right thumb. Mayfield has struggled since returning from that injury, completing 25 of 46 pass attempts (54.3 percent) for 307 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions while the Buccaneers have embraced a run-heavy attack.

short_comment: Smith recorded seven tackles (four solo) and an interception in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
long_comment: As a team, the Bucs picked off Caleb Williams four times Sunday night, but it still wasn't enough to propel Tampa Bay to a win. Smith now has two picks over his last three games and is up to 50 tackles (26 solo), three pass breakups and a forced fumble across nine starts this season. He has a chance to best last season's career-high 100 tackles in 2026.

short_comment: McCollum recorded five tackles (four solo) and two interceptions in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
long_comment: The cornerback has been on an absolute heater in the interceptions department, as he's now recorded at least one pick in three straight games. After picking off Bryce Young and Michael Penix in back-to-back games, McCollum got Caleb Williams twice in Week 9. The four interceptions are a new career high for the fifth-year defensive back, who is now up to 35 tackles (28 solo), 11 pass breakups and a fumble recovery across nine games this season.

short_comment: Anzalone posted two solo tackles and an interception during the Buccaneers' 27-24 loss to the Bears in Week 9.
long_comment: The Buccaneers picked off Caleb Williams four times, which included Anzalone's pick late in the third quarter that set up Tampa Bay in Chicago territory. Anzalone recorded four interceptions over his first nine NFL seasons, but he's already up to four picks in 2026, three of which have come over his last two outings. He enters the Week 10 bye with 44 tackles (19 solo), including 1.0 sacks, through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Trotter recorded eight tackles (five solo) during the Buccaneers' 27-24 loss to the Bears in Week 9.
long_comment: Trotter led the Buccaneers in tackles in Week 9, when he played 59 of 61 defensive snaps (96.7 percent). The rookie second-rounder has logged at least six stops in each of the first eight games of the regular season, and he enters the Week 10 bye with 76 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and three pass defenses (including a pick-six).

short_comment: Johnson played all 17 of his snaps on special teams and recorded one tackle in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
long_comment: Johnson, a reserve wide receiver, has been used almost exclusively on special teams through his two-plus seasons in Tampa Bay. He's logged just 15 total snaps on offense through nine games in 2026, recording a three-yard reception on two targets. Johnson leads the Buccaneers with 14 kickoff returns for 389 yards, but he didn't see any runback opportunities in Week 9 while Sean Tucker handled those duties.

short_comment: Hurst failed to haul in his lone target during the Buccaneers' 27-24 loss to the Bears on Sunday.
long_comment: For a third consecutive game, the rookie third-rounder didn't record a catch while seeing only one target. Of more concern was the fact that Hurst was on the field for only one offensive snap in Week 9 after logging at least 25 offensive snaps in each of the first eight games of the regular season. That lack of offensive playing time coincided with the return of Emeka Egbuka, although Hurst also saw less snaps than Chris Godwin (62), Tez Johnson (52) and even David Sills (six), although Sills was cut by the Buccaneers on Tuesday. With the Buccaneers on a bye for Week 10, Hurst will look for better results in Week 11 against the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 22.

short_comment: Johnson caught two passes for 76 yards on five targets in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
long_comment: Johnson accounted for the Bucs' longest play of the game, producing a 58-yard catch-and-run to lead the team in receiving yards. Johnson has been working as the Bucs' WR3 behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin, with rookie Ted Hurst mixing in for sub-package snaps. Johnson isn't a particularly exciting fantasy bet.

short_comment: Tucker didn't log any offensive snaps in a loss to the Bears on Sunday. He returned four kickoffs for 92 yards.
long_comment: It was the second straight week in which Tucker went without an offensive snap. That's happened despite Tampa Bay going to the ground plenty during that span. Perhaps not coincidentally, Tucker has begun working as a kick returner during the two-game stretch. It appears he's not going to get many opportunities on offense as long as Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell are healthy.

short_comment: McLaughlin converted all three of his field-goal attempts and both of his extra-point tries during Tampa Bay's loss to the Bears on Sunday.
long_comment: McLaughlin had a solid outing despite the loss, although all three of his field goals came from within 35 yards. Across his first nine outings of the season, the 30-year-old has yet to miss a kick, converting on all 22 field-goal attempts and all 18 extra-point tries.

short_comment: Otton caught four of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
long_comment: The tight end saw a team-high eight targets, drawing a 26.7 percent target share from Baker Mayfield. It still didn't translate into much in the box score, as Otton remains without a touchdown through nine games. He's turned 38 targets into 23 catches for 211 yards this season and is a low-floor fantasy option most weeks.

long_comment: out

short_comment: Head coach Todd Bowles said Monday that the Buccaneers "will try and lessen the load" on Irving following their Week 10 bye, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.
long_comment: Though he hasn't shown any signs of wearing down while he's averaged a healthy 4.9 yards per tote through the Buccaneers' first nine games, Irving has already amassed 167 carries -- fourth-most in the NFL -- and would be on pace for a career-high 315 over the course of a 17-game schedule. Given the success they've found on the ground in recent weeks, the Buccaneers could continue to embrace a run-first attack, but expect Irving to cede a bit more work to backups Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker as Tampa Bay aims to keep their top back healthy for the long haul.

short_comment: Head coach Todd Bowles suggested Monday that McMillan (knee) isn't likely to immediately return to action following the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.
long_comment: While Bowles indicated that linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) has decent odds of playing in the Buccaneers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Lions, the coach was less optimistic about McMillan's chances of being ready to play in Week 11. The Buccaneers have yet to open McMillan's 21-day practice window, after he was placed on injured reserve Sept. 30 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, which was an aggravation of a previous injury. Bowles noted that McMillan underwent a medical procedure on the knee shortly after landing on IR and is still dealing with some discomfort.

short_comment: Godwin caught two of three targets for 16 yards and added a 12-yard rush during Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
long_comment: Godwin has now gone back-to-back weeks without reeling in at least three passes after having done so in each of Tampa Bay's first seven contests this year. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 50 receiving yards or reach the end zone over nine games so far during the 2026 campaign, and he will remain an unappealing fantasy option when the Buccaneers return to action in Week 11 against the Lions.

short_comment: Gainwell rushed five times for 16 yards and caught all three of his targets for 60 yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
long_comment: Most of Gainwell's 76 scrimmage yards came on a 44-yard catch. He has 304 scrimmage yards over the past three games after recording just 122 scrimmage yards across his first six outings for the Buccaneers. Bucky Irving rushed for two touchdowns Sunday and remains the top option in Tampa Bay's backfield, but Gainwell has started to make the most of his change-of-pace role in the Buccaneers' run-heavy offense. Gainwell will try to pick up where he left off in Week 11 against the Lions after a Week 10 bye.

short_comment: Egbuka (foot) caught three of five targets for 38 yards and added a one-yard run in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
long_comment: Egbuka returned from a two-game absence during which he was in concussion protocol in addition to dealing with a foot injury. He tied for second on the team in targets behind Cade Otton's eight and finished third in receiving yards behind Tez Johnson (76) and Kenny Gainwell (60), as Baker Mayfield spread the ball around to complement Bucky Irving's two-touchdown effort on the ground. Egbuka hasn't exceeded 63 yards in seven appearances this season heading into Tampa Bay's Week 10 bye.

short_comment: Winfield (ankle) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday night's contest against the Bears.
long_comment: Winfield sustained an ankle injury late in the first half, and his night has now officially come to a premature end. With Winfield unavailable, Ifeatu Melifonwu will continue to operate as one of Tampa Bay's primary safeties versus Chicago.

short_comment: Wirfs (toe) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Bears.
long_comment: Wirfs appeared on Thursday's injury report as a non-participant with a toe injury. The star left tackle managed to upgrade to limited for Friday's session. The upgrade to limited participation was enough to clear Wirfs of any injury designation, and the veteran protector is all set to suit up for Sunday's contest.

short_comment: Parrish registered seven total tackles (four solo) and two passes defensed, including an interception, during Sunday's 16-0 win over Atlanta.
long_comment: Parrish was able to notch multiple passes defensed for the fifth straight game, and he was able to reel in his second interception of the year, jumping in front of a short pass from Falcons quarterback Michael Penix in the second quarter. The cornerback has now compiled 36 total tackles (30 solo) and 13 passes defensed, including two interceptions, over seven contests so far during the 2026 regular season.

long_comment: out

long_comment: out

short_comment: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Monday that he's hopeful that Tate (shoulder) will return to action Week 11 versus the Cowboys, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Even with the benefit of a Week 9 bye, Tate still wound up being sidelined for a second straight game in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars on account of the shoulder injury. Though Saleh is optimistic that the rookie wideout will be ready to go for the Titans' upcoming game in Dallas, Tate will first need to return to practice in some fashion to make that a reality. Tate remained a non-participant in practice throughout Week 10 prep.

short_comment: Helm caught all four of his targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.
long_comment: After a career day last time out in Week 8 against the Bengals, Helm's box score looked more familiar against Jacksonville's stout defense. He's been held below 30 yards in eight of nine games this season and has yet to catch a touchdown. Helm is a member of the large bucket of low-floor TE2 options in fantasy.

short_comment: Spears rushed four times for 28 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. He turned one catch into zero yards on one target.
long_comment: After missing the previous two games with a knee injury, Spears returned to play 16 offensive snaps. Tony Pollard (41 snaps) remains the clear-cut lead back on this cellar-dwelling Tennessee team. Spears has minimal fantasy appeal now that Pollard survived the trade deadline and will finish out the season with the Titans.

short_comment: Ayomanor caught five of 10 targets for 79 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.
long_comment: While he wasn't particularly efficient with the volume, Ayomanor led the Titans in targets and receiving yards on the afternoon, , and the receptions and yardage were both career highs, with Carnell Tate (shoulder) sidelined and Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) exiting the contest early. If they both remain on the shelf in Week 11 against the Cowboys, Ayomanor figures to handle an increased role once again. The second-year WR sports an 18-290-1 line on 36 targets through nine games on the year.

short_comment: Pollard carried the ball nine times for 33 yards and caught eight of nine targets for 66 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.
long_comment: The veteran RB fell one yard short of reaching 100 scrimmage yards for a third straight game, and Pollard gave the Titans a brief glimmer of hope in the fourth quarter when he took a checkdown from Cam Ward 32 yards to the house, making the score 30-23. Pollard led the Titans in receptions as he produced season-best numbers through the air, and he could retain elevated usage as a pass catcher if top WRs Carnell Tate (shoulder) and Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) miss additional time. Pollard lines up for a potential revenge game in Week 11 against the Cowboys.

short_comment: Ward completed 28 of 39 passes for 231 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.
long_comment: The second-year QB kept his team in the game for three quarters, and Ward connected with Tony Pollard for a 32-yard catch-and-run TD on a checkdown in the fourth quarter that brought the Titans to within one score, only for the Jags to pull away late. Ward's production is slowly creeping up, and he's thrown for 535 yards over the last two games with a 4:1 TD:INT, 68.4 percent completion rate and 6.8 YPA, numbers which represent a big step up from the beginning of the season. He'll look to keep making progress in his development in Week 11 against a vulnerable Cowboys defense.

short_comment: Robinson is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Jaguars due to an ankle injury.
long_comment: The Titans were already without Carnell Tate (shoulder) Sunday, and the team's receiver depth took another hit when Robinson appeared to sustain the injury late in the third quarter. If Robinson is unable to check back into the contest, he'll finish the game with three catches for 10 yards on four targets.

short_comment: Adams has entered the league's concussion protocol and has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
long_comment: With Adams done for the day, Terrell Burgess and Isaiah Oliver are both in line for more defensive snaps in the secondary. Adams will need to clear the league's concussion protocol in order to play in Week 11 against the Cowboys on Nov. 22.

short_comment: The Titans signed Oliver from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
long_comment: Oliver had been elevated from the practice squad twice this season and logged seven tackles (three solo) and a defensed pass over 36 defensive snaps and 29 special-teams snaps. He'll now presumably work in a rotational role at safety on game days.

short_comment: Tennessee signed Zavala from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
long_comment: Zavala played for Carolina each of his first three NFL seasons and started 14 of the 34 games in which he appeared. He should serve in a rotational role at offensive guard for Tennessee.

short_comment: The Titans signed Morstead from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
long_comment: Morstead first worked as Tennessee's punter during Week 8 against Cincinnati. Following the team's Week 9 bye, Tommy Townsend (knee/Achilles) was placed on IR, clearing the way for Morstead to retain the punter role for at least the next four weeks.

short_comment: The Titans placed Townsend (knee/Achilles) on IR on Saturday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
long_comment: Townsend suffered a knee injury during the Week 7 loss to Cleveland and is also now dealing with an Achilles issue. His placement on IR means he'll be sidelined for at least four games. Thomas Morstead was signed by Tennessee from the practice squad to the active roster to take Townsend's role as the team's punter.

short_comment: The Titans elevated Restrepo from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: It's the second game in a row that Restrepo has been elevated to the 53-man roster, and he'll provide the Titans will extra depth at wide receiver in the absence of Carnell Tate (shoulder). Restrepo played 19 snaps on special teams and logged two solo tackles during the Titans' Week 8 overtime loss to the Bengals.

short_comment: The Titans placed Skoronski (hamstring) on injured reserve Saturday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Skoronski was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jaguars due to a hamstring injury that he picked up in Week 8 against the Bengals. Now that he's on IR, the fourth-year offensive lineman will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 14 against the Lions on Sunday, Dec. 13. James Hudson and Garrett Dellinger figure to be the top candidates to start at left guard in Skoronski's absence.

short_comment: Dike may have a significant role on offense with Carnell Tate (shoulder) ruled out for Sunday's game against Jacksonville.
long_comment: Tate also missed the previous game, before a Week 9 bye, when Dike caught five of six targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in a 43-36 overtime loss to Cincinnati. Dike played 83 percent of snaps in the contest, running more routes (33) than both Elic Ayomanor (30) and Calvin Ridley (22). The 70-percent route share was easily a season high for Dike, and his performance suggests a sizable role should be coming again this Sunday.

short_comment: Latham (finger) practiced in full Wednesday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
long_comment: Latham injured his finger in the fourth quarter of the Titans' Week 8 overtime loss to the Bengals. He had extra time to rest thanks to the Week 9 bye, and given his full participation in Wednesday's practice, Latham should suit up as the Titans' starting left guard for Sunday's AFC South showdown against the Jaguars.

short_comment: Harris (ankle) practiced in full Wednesday.
long_comment: The second-year cornerback was injured in the Week 8 overtime loss to the Bengals, but the bye came at the right time, and he appears to be ready to go for Sunday's date with the Jaguars. Harris has functioned as Tennessee's slot corner this season, so he figures to see plenty of Parker Washington in Week 10.

short_comment: The Titans placed Williams (groin) on injured reserve Monday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
long_comment: In a corresponding transaction, Tennessee activated linebacker Dorian Mausi from injured reserve. Williams won't be able to return to game action until Week 14 against the Lions at the earliest. In the meantime, Mausi figures to assume the small role Williams was occupying.

short_comment: Coach Dan Quinn said Monday that while the 21-day practice window for Croskey-Merritt (groin) hasn't been opened yet, he notes that the running back is "trending in the right direction," Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Croskey-Merritt landed on IR back on Oct. 19, but now that the running has missed the required four games his stint on the list entailed, he's eligible to return to practice once he's ready to do so. Quinn's comment Monday suggests that's not an imminent outcome, though Croskey-Merritt's Week 11 outlook could brighten by the time the Commanders' first injury report ahead of next Monday's game against the Bengals is posted. In Washington's latest game -- a Nov. 12 24-21 win over the Giants -- Rachaad White (11 carries, one catch) and Austin Ekeler (nine carries, four catches) handled the bulk of the team's rushing load in Week 10.

short_comment: Reaves recorded nine tackles (seven solo), one pass defense and one fumble recovery during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
long_comment: Reaves finished Thursday's game second on the Commanders in tackles behind rookie first-round linebacker Sonny Styles (13), and the former jumped on a loose ball caused by Frankie Luvu in the third quarter that stopped the Giants' red zone drive. Reaves has logged at least five stops in each of the first nine games of the regular season, and the veteran safety is up to 62 tackles (35 solo), four pass defenses and one fumble recovery on the year.

short_comment: Cross finished Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants with six tackles (one solo).
long_comment: Cross was one of three Commanders players who played all 65 defensive snaps during Thursday's win. He's posted at least six stops in each of his last three outings, and over that span, he has accumulated 23 tackles (12 solo), three pass defenses (including one interception) and one fumble recovery.

short_comment: Luvu recorded six tackles (two solo) and a forced fumble during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
long_comment: Luvu stopped the Giants' red zone drive in the third quarter after punching the ball out of the hands of Malik Nabers, and Jeremy Reaves jumped on the loose ball to secure the takeaway for the Commanders. Luvu has played every single snap in each of his last three games, and he has accumulated 51 tackles (21 solo), including 1.0 sacks, one pass defense, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery over his last six outings.

short_comment: Styles recorded 13 tackles (five solo) during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
long_comment: Styles once again led the Commanders in stops while playing every single defensive snap. He has logged exactly 13 tackles in four of his last five games and is up to 80 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, four pass defenses (including one interception) and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games. Styles' 80 combined tackles are third-most among rookies behind Anthony Hill (neck) (82) and Arvell Reese (81).

short_comment: Stevens made his only field-goal attempt and was successful on all three of his extra-point tries in Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants.
long_comment: Stevens began the scoring in the contest with a 46-yard field goal early in the second period. That ended up being his only FG try of the game, but he made all three of his PATs. Stevens continued what has been a mostly fine rookie campaign -- he's made 17 of 20 field-goal attempts, with all three of his misses coming from 50-plus yards. However, he's just 15-for-18 on point-after tries.

short_comment: Sinnott caught all four of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown Thursday in a 24-21 victory against the Giants.
long_comment: Sinnott gave the Commanders a lead just before halftime when he reeled in a one-yard touchdown from Jayden Daniels. It was his first TD of the season and the third of his career. Sinnott's four grabs came out of nowhere, as he'd logged just one catch on two targets through his first eight games of the season. He also ranked third among Washington tight ends Thursday with 24 offensive snaps -- behind Chig Okonkwo (41) and John Bates (28) -- so fantasy managers probably don't need to go rushing to the waiver wire to pick him up. With that said, Sinnott may have earned himself more opportunities with Thursday's effort.

short_comment: Burks caught two of three targets for 27 yards Thursday in a 24-21 win over the Giants.
long_comment: Burks missed Week 9 due to a foot injury but was able to limit his absence to one game. The veteran wideout logged a 60 percent offensive snap share, third among Washington wideouts behind Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams. Burks has a chance to take on a larger role in the Commanders' passing game with Terry McLaurin (knee) lost for the season, though Diggs and Williams may be better bets for weekly production given their higher spots in the pecking order.

short_comment: Williams secured both targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
long_comment: Williams was a distant second to Stefon Diggs in receiving yards for the Commanders on the night, but like the latter, the former was on the receiving end of one of Jayden Daniels' three touchdown passes. Williams scored from 31 yards out just past the midway point of the third quarter, his first touchdown since way back in Week 1 against the Eagles. Williams hasn't been able to fully take advantage of the absence of Terry McLaurin (knee, IR) as of yet, but Thursday's score is certainly an encouraging sign heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.

short_comment: Ekeler rushed nine times for 26 yards and brought in all four targets for 26 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
long_comment: As his final line indicates, Ekeler retained a solid level of involvement in the narrow win, logging a season-high 13 touches. He posted a new season high in receiving yards along the way, and the veteran back has proven to be a solid complement to Rachaad White while Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin, IR) has been sidelined. However, with the latter potentially set to return as soon as Week 11's home matchup against the Bengals, Ekeler could be headed to a reduced role.

short_comment: White rushed 11 times for 47 yards and brought in one of two targets for five yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
long_comment: White led the Commanders' ground attack once again, posting a team high in rushing yards and tying for the team lead in rush attempts with Jayden Daniels. The veteran back wasn't as involved as usual as a receiver, however, capping the overall quality of his fantasy performance. White also could see Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin, IR) make his return for a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23, a development that would likely relegate the former to a complementary role he'd presumably share with Austin Ekeler.

short_comment: Diggs secured six of 10 targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
long_comment: Diggs paced the Commanders across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his 32-yard catch-and-run touchdown grab over the middle with under a minute remaining sealed the win for Washington. Diggs tied a season high with his catch total while setting a new 2026 high-water mark in receiving yards and targets as well, and the veteran wideout should retain a prominent role throughout the second half of the season with Terry McLaurin (IR, knee) out the rest of the way in 2026. Diggs next takes aim at the Bengals' inconsistent secondary in a Week 11 home matchup on Monday night, Nov. 22.

short_comment: Daniels completed 23 of 33 passes for 249 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions and rushed 11 times for 28 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
long_comment: It was a up-and-down night for Daniels in the narrow division win, as the third-year quarterback's pair of fourth-quarter interceptions threatened to derail Washington's fortunes. Daniels had the Commanders up by a 17-14 score just past the midway point of the third quarter after tossing one- and 31-yard touchdown passes to Ben Sinnott and Antonio Williams, respectively. However, Daniels subsequently squandered one scoring opportunity by throwing interceptions on back-to-back possessions in the fourth quarter, the first at the Giants' two-yard line. He ultimately made up for it with his game-winning 32-yard scoring strike to Stefon Diggs, marking the quarterback's first three-TD-pass tally of the season. Daniels is up to 1,499 passing yards and a 10:2 TD:INT alongside 280 rushing yards and another pair of scores heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.

short_comment: Okonkwo (back) returned to Thursday's eventual 24-21 win at the Giants, finishing with four catches (on eight targets) for 24 yards.
long_comment: Okonkwo exited in the second quarter due to a back injury, but he was back out there on the field after halftime and was the target on both of Jayden Daniels' two interceptions with less than six minutes remaining in the contest. Overall, Okonkwo's eight targets marked a season high, but he also mustered his fewest receiving yards since Week 4. He'll look to build upon his season-long line of 27-263-0 on 39 targets in the Commanders' next game Monday, Nov. 23 versus the Bengals.

short_comment: Jefferson caught five of seven targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams.
long_comment: With Terry McLaurin (knee) and Treylon Burks (foot) out for the Commanders, Jefferson played 36 of 62 offensive snaps and ran 25 routes on Jayden Daniels' 42 dropbacks. The veteran wideout was signed to the active roster from the practice squad two weeks ago and led the team in receiving against Los Angeles. If Burks needs to miss more time, Jefferson could again have a role in three-wide sets Thursday night against the Giants.

short_comment: Newton (pectoral) is active for Sunday's game against the Rams.
long_comment: The 24-year-old was reinstated from injured reserve Saturday but was still officially questionable to play Sunday versus Los Angeles. Newton is ready to make his season debut after recovering from surgery to repair a torn pectoral muscle in August.

short_comment: The Commanders placed Brown (calf) on injured reserve Saturday.
long_comment: Brown will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a calf injury during Thursday's practice. With Treylon Burks (foot) also ruled out, Van Jefferson and Luke McCaffrey could see increased usage on offense during Sunday's matchup versus the Rams.
